verses.text: In the land of Uz there lived a man whose name was Job. He was a man of complete integrity. He respected God and so he avoided doing evil things.
Now Job had seven sons and three daughters.
He owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 1,000 oxen, and 500 donkeys. He also had many servants. Job was richer than anyone else who lived in the area east of the Jordan River.
Job’s sons often held feasts in their homes. Whenever any of them held a feast, he would invite all of his brothers and sisters to share the meal with him.

After all of the sons had each held a feast, Job would gather his children together. He would ask Yahweh to cleanse them from any action they might have committed during their feasting that would have made them unacceptable to him. He would get up early in the morning, kill animals, and burn them on the altar {as sacrifices}, one for each {of his children}. {For} Job {always said}, “Perhaps my children have sinned by saying something evil about God in their thoughts. {If they have, I need to ask God to forgive them.}” Job did this after each time his sons had all hosted feasts.
One day the angels came and gathered together in front of Yahweh, and Satan came too.
Yahweh asked Satan, “Where have you just come from?”
Yahweh said to Satan, “Have you noticed Job, who worships me? I mention him because no one else on earth has such complete integrity as he does. He respects me and so he refuses to do anything evil.”
Satan replied to Yahweh, “Job only worships you because of what you have done for him.
You have always protected him, his family, and everything he owns. You make him succeed in whatever work he does. As a result, he has built very large herds of livestock.
But if you attack what he owns and take it away, he will certainly curse you in front of everyone.”
Yahweh replied to Satan, “All right, I permit you to take away everything that he has. But do not harm him in his own body.”
One day after that, Job’s sons and daughters were attending a feast at the home of the oldest brother.
{While they were doing that,} a messenger arrived at Job’s home. He told Job, “Your oxen were plowing the fields and your donkeys were grazing nearby.

But a group of men, Sabeans, came and attacked us. They killed all of your servants who were working in the fields. They took away all the oxen and donkeys! I am the only one who has escaped to come and tell you what happened.”

While he was still talking to Job, another messenger arrived. He said to Job, “Lightning from the sky struck and killed all the sheep and all the men who were taking care of them! I am the only one who has escaped to come and tell you what happened.”

While he was still talking to Job, a third messenger arrived. He said to Job, “Three groups of robbers from the region of Chaldea came and attacked us. They stole all the camels and killed all the men who were taking care of them. I am the only one who has escaped to come and tell you what happened.”
While he was still talking to Job, a fourth messenger arrived. He said to Job: “Your sons and daughters were feasting in the home of their oldest brother.

Suddenly a very strong wind came from the desert and struck the house. The house collapsed on your sons and daughters and killed them all! I am the only one who has escaped to come and tell you what happened.”
Then Job stood up and tore his robe and shaved his head {because he was very sad}. Then he lay down on the ground to worship God.

He said, “When I was born, I was wearing no clothes. When I die, I will not take any clothes with me. It is Yahweh who gave me everything that I possessed, and it is Yahweh who has taken it all away. I find no fault with Yahweh.”
So in spite of all the things that had happened to him, Job did not sin by saying that what God had done was wrong.
On another day, the angels came again and gathered together in front of Yahweh. Satan also came again.
Yahweh asked Satan, “Where have you come from {this time}?” Satan replied, “I have come from the earth, where I was traveling around {to see what was happening}.”

Yahweh asked Satan, “Have you noticed that Job continues to worship me? I mention him again because no one else on earth has such complete integrity as he does. He respects me, and so he refuses to do anything evil. He still does this even though you persuaded me to {permit you to} attack him for no reason.”

Satan replied to Yahweh, “Job still worships you because he is glad you destroyed his herds and family rather than destroying him. People will give up everything they have in order to save their own lives.
But if you harm his body, he will certainly curse you in front of everyone!”
Yahweh replied to Satan, “All right, I permit you to harm his body. But you must leave him alive.”
Satan {agreed and he} left. He went and caused Job to suffer from very painful boils all over his body.
Job took a piece of broken pottery and scraped the boils on his skin. He sat down in a pile of ashes {outside the city}.
His wife said to him, “You should not still be loyal to God! You should curse God and then go ahead and die.”

But Job replied, “You are talking the way people talk who do not know God. We should be willing to receive whatever God sends us.” So in spite of all the things that had happened to him, Job did not sin by saying that what God had done was wrong.

Job had some good and wise friends. One of them was Eliphaz from the town of Teman. Another was Bildad, who was a Shuhite. A third friend was Zophar from the town of Naamah. These men heard about the terrible things that had happened to Job. So they each left their homes and went together to visit Job to comfort him sincerely.

But when they saw Job from a distance, they almost did not recognize him. They wailed loudly, they all tore their clothing, and they threw dust into the air that settled on their heads. {They did these things to demonstrate how sorry they were for Job.}
Then they sat on the ground with Job for seven days. {During that time} none of them said anything to him, out of respect for how greatly he was suffering.
At the end of those seven days, Job started speaking. He cursed the day when he was born.
He said,
“I wish that the day of my birth had never existed! {I feel the same way about} the night when my mother conceived me.
I wish that there would only be darkness on that day {so that it would not even be a day}. I wish that God in heaven would not care about that day and so not make the sun shine on it.
I wish that that day were only darkness, with clouds blocking out the sunlight and many other things also making it very dark.

I wish that the moon and stars would not shine on the night when my mother conceived me. I wish that the day of my birth was not part of any month. Indeed, I wish that it was not a day in the year at all.
I mean it—I wish that no mother would ever again bear a child on that date. I wish that no one would ever again rejoice {over a child’s birth} on that date.
There are magicians who know how to agitate the chaos monster. I want them to curse the day of my birth!

I wish that the stars that shone early in the morning of that day would never shine again. I wish that it would never become light on that day. I wish that not even the first rays of the rising sun would appear on that day.
I wish that day did not exist, because my mother gave birth to me on that day, and because I became alive, I have now experienced all these terrible things.
I wish that I had died right after my mother gave birth to me! I wish I had stopped breathing after being alive for only a short time!
I wish that my mother had never held me on her lap and nursed me!
If I had died shortly after my mother gave birth to me, I would now be resting peacefully among all the other people who had died.
{I would be resting} with great kings and their advisers. They built beautiful tombs on spacious grounds {and are now resting in them}.
Or {I would be resting} with princes who owned great quantities of gold and silver.
I wish that I had died in my mother’s womb and never lived for even a moment. Then people would have buried me privately.
After wicked people die, they do not cause any more trouble. That allows the people whom they were oppressing to rest.
Those who were prisoners all rest peacefully {after they die}. They no longer have slave drivers ordering them around.
Everyone, whether rich or poor, goes to the realm of the dead. Those who were slaves no longer have to obey their masters.
God should not allow those who are suffering greatly like me to continue to remain alive! God should not allow those who are very miserable to live!
They long to die, but they do not die. They desire to die more than people desire to find buried treasure.
{God should not give life in the first place} to people who are very happy when they finally die!
God should not give life to people if he is going to keep them from knowing what to do or from understanding what is really happening to them!
I am wishing that I were dead because now I cry so much that I cannot eat. I just keep groaning loudly.
There were things that I always worried might happen to me. Those things have now happened!
I really have no peace of mind at all. My troubles keep disturbing me.”
Then Eliphaz, Job’s friend from the town of Teman, replied to what Job had said. Eliphaz said,
“Will you please allow me to say something to you? I feel compelled to speak to you.
You yourself have given good advice to many people. You have encouraged people who were discouraged.
When people were struggling, you were able to say the right thing to help them. You enabled them to be brave again.
But now that you yourself are suffering, you have become discouraged. You are not facing your troubles bravely {as you have helped others to do}.
You should be confident because you honor God. You should be hopeful because you conduct yourself with integrity.
Think about this: God does not destroy people who are innocent! No, God never kills people who are doing what is right!
I know from experience that this is true: When people plan to do bad things to others, those bad things happen to them instead.
God becomes very angry with them {because of the wrong things they plan to do}, and so God commands that they will die, and they do die.
Wicked people may boast and threaten, but God destroys them.

Those wicked people will have nothing in the end, like lions that starve to death because God keeps them from catching any prey. Different relatives will have to take care of the children of those wicked people, as if they were lion cubs whose parents caught no prey and they had to separate from each other in order to search for food.
I once heard a message that someone came and whispered to me.
One night I fell deeply asleep and had a dream that made me very perplexed.
I was so scared that I started to shake all over.
Then a spirit slid into view right in front of me! This caused the hair on the back of my neck to stand straight up.
The spirit stopped there, but I could not see what it really looked like. However, I knew that there was some being in front of me. At first it did not speak, but then it said,
‘No human being can be more righteous than God. No person can be better than his Creator.
Consider this: God recognizes that even his own angels may not always do what is right. If they do not act wisely, he corrects them.
So God is even more careful to discipline human beings, knowing how very frail they are.
{Humans are so fragile that} they can be here today and gone tomorrow. {And humans are so insignificant that} a person can die, never to return to earth, and no one will even notice.
Humans are {fragile,} like tents that collapse if someone pulls up their stakes. And they may live their whole lives on earth without ever learning to be wise.’
If you ask someone to judge between you and God, no one will agree to do that for you. Not even an angel would have the authority or wisdom to judge your case.

People who do not respect God get angry with God {instead of considering how they have sinned}. Naïve people resent God {when they do not get what they think they deserve}. {Their anger and resentment lead them to disobey God, so that} God punishes them severely and even kills them. So respect God and do not be naïve!
I have seen foolish people who seemed to be successful. But immediately I recognized that they would not prosper for long.
Their children are never safe. They always lose to their opponents in court because no one defends them.

People who do not respect God are not able to harvest the crops that they plant. Poor people come and claim the grain—right to the edges of the field! Yes, poor people see their crops and are glad to have them.
After all, trouble does not come out of nowhere.
No, people cause trouble for themselves throughout their lives. This is as certain as the fact that sparks shoot up from a fire.
If I were suffering as you are, I would ask God for help and trust God to help me.
God does great things that we can not understand. We can not even count the marvelous things that God does.
God is the one who sends rain onto the earth so that it waters our fields.
God defends people who are humble. He gives widows safe places to live.
God keeps devious people from being able to do what they plan.
When people try cleverly to make others suffer, God makes this cause suffering for them instead. When people try to trick others, God shows that it is a trick before it can fool the others.

God keeps wicked people from knowing how to fulfill their plans. It is as if the wicked people are always in the dark, even during the day, and they need to feel around with their hands to try to find where to go.
When powerful people threaten or accuse weak people, God rescues the weak people. He keeps the powerful people from harming them.
{Because they know that God will help them,} poor people can confidently expect that good things will happen to them. God proves that they are innocent when people accuse them falsely.
Consider this: Anyone whom God corrects is better off because of it. So you should be thankful that God is disciplining you.
You should be thankful because God allows people to suffer {in order to correct them} and then he restores them.
Whenever you are in trouble, God will keep rescuing you. God will keep bad things from happening to you.
When there is little food to eat, God will not allow you to starve to death. When there is war, God will not allow your enemies to kill you.
God will protect you when people say bad things about you. God will protect you from things that could badly harm you.
You will not worry about things like that or about not having enough to eat. You will not be afraid that wild animals will hurt you,
because you will be confident that those wild animals will not attack you. You will not have big rocks in your fields that make plowing difficult.
You will know that things will go well for you in your home. When you check on your animals, you will see that they are all there.
You will be certain that you will have many descendants. They will be as numerous as blades of grass.
You will live a long life, like grain that grows to become fully ripe before it is harvested.

I can assure you that my friends and I have thought carefully about these things. We know that they are true, so please pay careful attention to what I have said! You also will realize that it is true.”
Then Job replied to Eliphaz and the others. He said,
“If I could put all my troubles and misery on a scale and weigh them,
they would certainly be heavier than all the sand along the ocean shores. That is why I spoke very rashly about the day when I was born.

It is as if Almighty God had shot me with arrows. It is as if those arrows had poison on their tips and that poison had gone into my spirit. The things that God has done to me are like soldiers lined up to attack me.

Just as a wild donkey does not complain by braying when it has plenty of grass to eat, and an ox does not complain by bellowing when it has food to eat, I would not complain if you were really helping me.
People use salt to help them eat food that has little taste. People do that with the white of an egg, for example. I have been saying how I feel in order to help me deal with my situation.
But regarding food itself, I actually do not want to eat at all, because my troubles are making me too upset to eat.
I wish that God would do for me what I have asked of him:
I wish that God would agree to let me die! God is certainly able to end my life.
If he did that, I would be comforted: I would know that in spite of the unrelenting pain I had suffered, I would still always have obeyed God’s commands.
I do not have the strength to endure until these troubles are over. I have nothing to look forward to, so I do not want to live any longer!
I am not strong like stone, my body is not sturdy like bronze, so I will not be able to endure these troubles for a long time.
I am no longer able to help myself. My troubles are keeping me from doing that.
When a man has many troubles, his friends should be kind to him, even if he stops honoring Almighty God.
But you, my friends, have not helped me. You are like streams in the wilderness that travelers cannot depend on, because they leave their channels empty in the dry season.
These streams are full of water when the melting ice and snow make them overflow,
but when the dry season comes, there is no water flowing in those streams, and the channels dry up.
Merchant caravans turn off the road to search for water. {However, there is no water in those stream beds, so} the merchants die in the desert.
The men in those caravans searched for some water because they were sure that they would find some.
They were very disappointed, because they had been sure that they would find water. They traveled a long distance to the stream bed, but there was no water in it.
Similarly, you three have not helped me at all! You have seen that terrible things have happened to me, and you are not helping me, because you are afraid that God might do similar things to you.
{After I lost all my wealth,} I did not ask any of you to give me money. I did not plead with any of you to spend some of your money to help me.
I never asked any of you to rescue me from my enemies. No, I did not ask you to save me from people who were oppressing me.
Answer me now, and then I will be quiet; tell me what wrong things I have done!
I would be willing to listen to what you had to say, even if it were painful, as long as it was helpful. But though you are trying to correct me, you are not really helping me at all.
I am a man who has nothing to hope for, but you try to correct me, and you think what I say is as useless as the wind!
In fact, you are treating me as callously as if you were gambling for an orphan or arguing over the price of a friend you were selling into slavery!
Please look at me! I will not lie while I am talking straight to you.
Please stop saying that I have sinned! Stop criticizing me unfairly! You should realize that I have not done anything wrong.
You must not think that I am lying! I know what is right to say and what is wrong to say.
Life is very difficult for all of us on this earth! Like manual laborers, our days are long and hard.
We are like slaves who keep wanting to be in the cool of evening. We are like workers who have to wait to be paid.
Like a slave, I am enduring a time when it feels useless to be alive. I have been experiencing many miserable nights.
When I go to bed I say, ‘I hope I will be able to sleep for a long time!’ But I never really get to sleep. I am restless right through to the morning.
My body is covered with maggots and dirt; pus oozes out of my open sores.
I am running out of days faster than a shuttle releases yarn into a loom, and I have no reason to hope that my life will end well.
God, remember that my life will soon end. {I do not think that} I will ever be happy again.
God, you see me now, but {after I die,} you will not see me anymore. You may look for me then, but {you will not find me, because} I will not exist.
Just as a cloud never appears in the sky again once it fades, so when people die and go to the place where dead people are, they never return to earth.
They never return and live in their houses again.
So I will say everything I want to say. I will speak because I am so upset. I will complain because I am so bitter.
God, you do not need to watch what I am doing so closely! I am not a dangerous sea monster!
Sometimes I think that if I could just go to sleep, I would stop suffering; my pain would be less while I was sleeping.
But then you make me have terrible nightmares!
And I wish someone would kill me by choking me so that I would not have to stay alive {and suffer so much}.
I hate being alive {and suffering so much}! I do not want to live any longer! Stop afflicting me, because I will only be alive for a short time.
We human beings are not very important! You should not think that we are so important that you need to pay attention to what we do.
You do not need to check every morning to see what we are doing! You do not need to evaluate us at every moment!
I wish you would stop watching me and leave me alone for at least a little while!
You watch me constantly, but if I sin, that certainly does not harm you! I feel as if I am your target and that you are shooting at me! You act as if I am bothering you all the time!
If I have done wrong things, you could just forgive me. I am going to die soon. When I do, then if you decide you want us to be friends, it will be too late, because I will be dead.”
Then Bildad, Job’s friend who was a Shuhite, responded to Job. He said,
“Job, you should not continue to talk like this. You are saying a lot of things, but they are not sensible.
God always does things fairly. Yes, Shaddai always does what is right.
Your children sinned against God. This is evident, because God has punished them for the evil things they did.
But as for you, you should pray to God. Yes, you should ask Shaddai to help you.
If you are genuinely good, then God will certainly do something good for you. He will give you back the abundant prosperity that good people have.
God would make you so wealthy later in life that it would seem as if you were not very prosperous before!
You should really consider the wise teachings of the people who lived before us. Yes, you should think about what our ancestors learned about life.

I advise you to consider the wisdom of our ancestors because we have only been alive for a short time and we know very little. This is because our time here on the earth is very short, like a shadow that appears briefly and then goes away.
But if you consider the wisdom of our ancestors, you will learn useful things. Indeed, you will learn very profound things.
Papyrus certainly does not grow away from marshland. No, reeds certainly cannot grow where there is no water.
If their water dries up while they are blossoming, they wither, while plants that do have water keep flourishing.
People who do not pay attention to God are like those reeds. Such people hope for good things, but they do not get them.
Godless people confidently expect good things to happen to them, but those things do not happen. Godless people trust certain other people to help them, but those others prove unreliable.

Godless people think they are secure because they are wealthy, but ultimately they can not rely on their wealth for security. When they begin to fail despite their wealth, they try to preserve their status, but they fail anyway.
Godless people are like plants that formerly flourished in abundant sunshine, whose branches once spread out over the ground.
Godless people are like plants whose roots once twisted securely around piles of stones and clung tightly to rocks.

But a person can still pull a plant completely out of the ground even if it is that healthy and securely rooted. Then it will be as if the plant was never there in the first place. People who do not pay attention to God will perish just as completely.
So people who do not pay attention to God will be sad in the end. Other people will come and take their places.
So I tell you, Job, that God will help you if you do what is right. But God will not help you if you do what is wrong.
God can still make you happy, yes, very happy.
{When God blesses you,} everyone who opposed you will be very ashamed. God will completely destroy wicked people.”
Then Job replied to Bildad and the others. He said,
“I certainly know that what you have said is true. But a person can not prove that he has done the right thing {and that God should not punish him}.
If someone wanted to argue with God about that, God would ask him many questions and that person would not be able to answer any of them!
God thinks very deeply and he is very powerful. No one who has tried to argue against him has ever been able to win.
God moves mountains {in earthquakes} without anyone knowing in advance what he is going to do. God knocks down mountains when he is angry.
God causes earthquakes far below the surface of the earth that shake the ground and make it move.
On some days, God makes it so cloudy that people can not see the sun in the sky. On some nights, God makes it so cloudy that people can not see the stars shining.
God created the sky all by himself. God defeated the forces of chaos {so that he could make an orderly universe}.
God arranged the stars in the sky to make constellations such as the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades. God arranged stars into many other constellations as well.
God does amazing things that people can not understand. God does more marvelous things than people are able to count.
If God passed by where I was, I would not be able to see him. Yes, he might be going by, but I would not notice him.
If God wants to take something away, no one can stop him from doing that. No one can require God to defend what he is doing.
God would continue to be angry {even if someone tried to calm him down}. {No one can oppose him;} he {even} defeated the forces of Rahab, the great sea monster.
So I could hardly think of the right words to say in order to argue a case against God!
Even if I were innocent, I would not be able to argue a case against him. All I could do would be to ask God, as my judge, to be merciful to me.
Even if he agreed to hear my case, I would not believe that he was genuinely considering my arguments.
He keeps causing troubles that batter me. He hurts me many times for no good reason.
He causes me to suffer all the time. It is as if he will not even let me get my breath again {before he causes the next disaster}.

Suppose I did make a case against him. And suppose the winner would be the one who was stronger. Then he would win, because he is far stronger than I am. And it would not matter who was right, since no one could make him obey what a judge decided.
Even though I was innocent, he would find grounds in what I said to punish me. Even though I had not done anything wrong, he would still decide, based on what I said, that I was guilty.
I have not done anything wrong, {but that does not matter anymore because} I do not care what happens to me. I do not care whether I live or die.
God punishes everyone the same way. As I have been saying, God destroys everyone whether they have done wrong or not.
When people experience disaster and it causes them to die suddenly, God laughs when he sees them suffer, even if they are innocent.

God has allowed wicked people to control what happens to everyone else. It is as though God has caused judges not to be able to judge fairly. If it is not God who has done that, who, then, has done it?
I am approaching the end of my life more quickly than a messenger runs to bring news. It is as if the days of my life are running away from me. Good things do not happen to me.
My life is going by very rapidly, as fast as a sailing boat made from reeds, as fast as an eagle swooping down to seize an animal.
If I decide that I will just forget what I am complaining about, if I decide to stop looking sad and try to be cheerful,
I still become afraid again because I know that God does not consider me innocent and so I think that he will punish me.
He will condemn me anyway, so why should I keep trying in vain to defend myself?
If I washed my body with pure water from melted snow and cleansed my hands with strong soap {to show how innocent I am},
God would just throw me into a filthy pit {to show how guilty he considers me to be}. My body would become so dirty that it would be as if my own clothes did not want to be on it!
God is not a human, as I am, so I could not refute him to prove that I am innocent if we went together to have a trial in a courtroom.
There is no one to mediate, no one who has authority over both of us.
There is no one who could keep God from causing me to suffer, who could keep God from doing terrifying things that frighten me.
{If someone could protect me and judge between us,} I would declare that I am innocent without being afraid of God. But I can not do that now.
I am tired of living, so I will freely express everything I want to complain about {without worrying about what God will do to me}. Yes, I will say exactly how unhappy I am.
I will say to God, ‘If you are going to punish me, you should tell me what I have done wrong!’
You seem to think that it is all right to harm me and to abandon me, whom you created. But at the same time, you seem pleased to allow wicked people to do the things that they plan to do!
Certainly you know and understand more than what people can see with their eyes! {So you should understand my true motives and know that I am innocent.}
You do not live for only a short time as people do!
So you do not need to act as if you would run out of time if you did not discover all of my sins right away!

{You do not need to work hard to discover any sins that I may have committed, because} you know that I am not guilty. And there is no one who could help me get away from you {if you decided you should punish me}.
You personally created every single part of me. So it is not right for you to destroy someone whom you created yourself.
Please recall how you made me! You molded me the way people mold objects out of clay. If you destroy me, I will crumble into dust {and you will lose your marvelous creative work}.
You made me through a careful process, the way people carefully make cheese out of milk.
You attached my bones together with tendons, and then you covered them with flesh inside my skin.
You are the one who made me alive. {It seemed that} you were faithfully taking care of me. {It seemed that} you were protecting me.
But you kept secret what you were planning to do to me. I am certain that you were planning to do these things to me!
You were watching me to see if I would sin so that you could punish me for sinning.
If I am a wicked man, then I hope that terrible things will happen to me. But even if I am a good man, I must still act ashamed because you are punishing me as if I had sinned.

If I did act like the good man that I am, you would {conclude that you should punish me further and you would} hunt for me the way a lion hunts for some animal to kill. {When you caught me,} you would do even more things to harm me greatly.
You would claim that I had committed even more sins. You would become even more angry with me. You would keep punishing me in new ways.
God, you should not have allowed my mother to give birth to me! I wish that I had died at birth! Yes, I wish that my parents had never shown me to anyone.
I wish that I had never even existed! I wish that I had died at birth so that people had buried me right away.
I am not going to live very much longer! So please leave me alone and let me have a little peace.
{Let me have some peace now because} soon I will go to the place from which I will never return. In that place {where dead people go} it is always gloomy. Yes, it is very dark.
Yes, in that place it is very dark, the way it is in deep shadow. Things are very chaotic there. Even the small light that is there is like darkness.”
Then Zophar, Job’s friend from the town of Naamah, responded to Job. He said,
“I would like to respond to the long speech that you have just given. You talk a lot about how innocent you are, but that does not mean that you truly are innocent.
You have boasted that you are innocent, and I need to talk back in response. You have said disrespectful things about God. I need to tell you that you should be ashamed!
I need to correct you because you have told God, ‘I believe the right things, and you know that I have done the right things.’
If only God would speak and say something to correct you!

If only God would tell you the secrets that he knows because he is so wise! {You need to realize that} God knows far more than you do. If you could understand as God does, you would realize that God is punishing you less than you deserve!
You will never be able to understand God by thinking hard about him. No, you will never be able to find out everything about Shaddai.

God’s wisdom is so much greater than ours, it is as if it is higher than the sky. So there is nothing you can do to understand it all. It is as if God’s wisdom is deeper below the earth than the place where dead people go. So it is impossible for you to know it all.
There is so much to know about God that it is as if that knowledge is longer than the earth and wider than the ocean.
If God wants to arrest you and put you on trial, no one can stop him from doing that.
{God is a trustworthy judge} because he knows which people have bad character. When God sees people doing wicked things, he punishes them.
Some people simply have no understanding. They will become wise when humans start having wild donkeys as babies{—that is, never!}
Job, I urge you to repent humbly and pray sincerely to God.
If you have been doing evil things, stop doing them. If you do nothing wrong in any part of your life,
then you will be able to act as a person who is not ashamed of anything. You will be strong, and you will not be afraid of anything.
You will not be afraid, because you will forget all the bad things that happened to you. They will all be gone, like the water that flows away down a river.
Your life will be happy again. It will be as if the sun were shining on you as brightly as it shines at mid-day. You have had many troubles, but they will end, just as night ends when the sun rises.
You will feel safe because you will be confident that good things will happen to you. You will think about your life and realize that you can go to bed and sleep peacefully.
You will lie down to sleep and nothing will scare you. Many people will come and ask you to be kind to them.
But God will punish wicked people by making them die. They will not be able to escape from God’s punishment. They will hope to live, but they will die anyway.”
Then Job replied to Zophar and the others. He said,
“You are speaking as if you were the people to whom everyone should listen. You seem to believe that you are the only wise people who are now alive.
But I have as much good sense as you do. I am just as wise as you are. People certainly know, in general, the things that you have said.
Before, when I prayed to God for help, God would help me. But now{, because God is not helping me in my suffering,} other people laugh at me. I am righteous and I honor God, but they laugh at me!
People like you who have no troubles think that others are suffering because of their sins. You think that God is punishing us and that is why we are suffering.
Meanwhile, bandits get rich by robbing people. Those who defiantly disobey God live peacefully. Such people believe that God cannot stop them from doing what they want to do.

But if the wild animals could speak, and if you asked them {what they know about God}, they would tell you {that God is responsible when someone suffers as I am suffering}. If the birds could speak, and if you asked them {the same question}, they would tell you {the same thing}.
If the ground could talk, and if you asked it about God, or if fish could talk and you asked them, they too would tell you that God is responsible when people suffer.
All of them certainly know that it is Yahweh himself who has caused me to suffer.
He controls whether all living creatures live or die, including whether any person dies or continues to live.

We decide whether our food is good or bad by tasting it. In the same way, we think carefully about what we hear people say in order to decide whether it is good or bad advice. {I have listened carefully to you, and I have decided that you are giving me bad advice!}
Older people have usually become wise. Because they have lived a long time, they have learned many things.
God himself is wise and very powerful. He has good sense and he understands everything.
Indeed, if God tears something down, no one can build it back up again. If God puts someone in prison, no one can enable that person to escape.
Yes, God is so powerful that if he prevents rain from falling, then the water on the earth dries up. If God causes a lot of rain to fall, then water floods onto the land.
God is the one who is truly strong and wise. He does not let anyone get away with doing wrong or with convincing others to do wrong.
{God is so powerful that} he can remove royal advisors from their positions, and he can cause judges to become fools.
God can take away the ruling authority that kings have and make those kings become slaves instead.
God can remove priests from their positions and take the power away from those who have long ruled others.
God can cause trusted counselors not to know what to say, and he can cause wise elders no longer to have good sense.
God can cause princes to lose the respect of others, and he can cause those who are powerful to become weak.
God can enable people to understand things that are very difficult to understand.

God causes some nations to become very great, but later he destroys them. God enables some nations to enlarge their territory greatly, but later he allows others to conquer them and take their people away as prisoners.
He causes some human rulers to become foolish. As a result, they try one thing after another without success, as if they were lost in a desert without roads.
It is as if they were trying to feel their way in complete darkness. It is as if they were staggering around drunk.”
“I can assure you, my friends, that I already know everything that you have been telling me. Yes, I have heard and understood all that you have said.
I know everything that you know. I do not know less than you do.
But I would like to speak with Almighty God{, not with you}. I would like to convince him {that I am innocent}.

As for you, you are telling so many lies about me that other people can hardly recognize what I am really like. Your advice is so worthless that you are all like doctors who sell people useless medicine.
I wish that you would just stop talking. Then you would really seem to be wise!
Please pay attention to what I am telling you!
You are speaking on God’s behalf, but you are not telling the truth! You are speaking deceptively, but you think that you are helping God!
You are not being fair to me. Instead, you are acting as if you are God’s lawyers defending him in court!
If God investigates what you are doing, he will find that you are doing wrong. No, you can not deceive him as you might deceive a human being!
God would certainly rebuke you when he discovered that you were pretending to be fair but were actually being unfair.
He would certainly bring the full force of his power against you. That would make you very afraid of him!
You are quoting traditional sayings, but they have no value in my situation. Your arguments in support of your position are very easy for someone to refute.
So stop talking to me. Allow me to speak. I do not care what God does to me as a result of what I say.
I will be risking my life. I will be taking the chance that God will execute me for what I say. But I have good reason to do that.
Indeed, God might kill me {for starting to argue a case against him}, but I hope that he {would still judge me fairly after I die}. So I am going to defend my behavior to him in person.
I believe that arguing a case against God will actually help convince God that I am innocent. After all, no wicked person would dare to approach God personally.”
“God, listen very carefully to what I say. Pay attention to me as I speak.
Please pay careful attention because I will be defending myself by telling you things I have thought carefully about. I have examined myself, and I am convinced that I am innocent.
I do not believe that anyone could prove that what I am going to say is false. If I knew that it was false, I would not argue this case. I would accept dying {as my fair punishment}.
However, I must ask you to stop doing two things to me. Then I will be able to speak with you in person.
The first thing I ask is that you stop punishing me. The second thing I ask is that you stop scaring me.
{If you agree to stop punishing me and stop scaring me, then} go ahead and start questioning me, and I will respond. Or allow me to question you first, and then you respond to my questions.
Tell me what I have done that is wrong. Tell me what sins I have committed. Show me how I have disobeyed you.
I do not understand why you are avoiding me. I do not understand why you are treating me like your enemy.
I am as insignificant as a leaf that the wind blows, so you do not need to punish me {as if I were a dangerous criminal}. I am as unimportant as a bit of dry chaff, so you do not need to chase me.

{From the way I am suffering, it appears that you are punishing me because} you consider that I have done terrible things. It seems that you are punishing me even for the wrong things I did when I was young {and I did not know any better}.

It seems as if {you are judging me too strictly, as if} you had put chains on my feet {to keep me from going anywhere}. It feels as if you are watching everything that I do very closely. It is as if you will only let me do a few specific things.

{But you do not need to watch me so closely.} I am a mere human being with a body that is as fragile as rotten wood that is falling apart, as fragile a piece of cloth that the larvae of moths are eating.
Human beings live only a short time, and during that time they experience much trouble.
People live brief lives, like flowers that appear quickly but then wither and fall to the ground. Yes, people’s lives are temporary, like shadows that appear only for a short time.
God, you do not need to watch fragile humans so carefully. You do not need to judge everything that I do.
No one can make something that is acceptable to God out of something that is not acceptable to him.
You have decided how many days each human life will last. Yes, you have decided how many months each person will live. No one can live any longer than the time you have decided. Because this is true,
please stop watching people so closely. Give them relief so that they can live out their brief lives in peace.
Now even after people cut a tree down, it is possible for it to start growing again and make new branches.
Its roots in the ground may be very old, and its stump may be decaying,
but when rain falls on it, it may revive and send up shoots just as a young plant does.
But even the strongest people die. They grow weak and stop breathing, and then they are gone forever.
Just as water evaporates from a lake, and just as a riverbed dries up,
so people die and do not become alive again. Until the heavens do not exist any longer, people who die will not come back to life. No, no one will be able to make them alive again.

I wish that you, God, would put me safely in the place where dead people go and forget about me. That way I would not suffer any more until you were no longer angry with me. I wish that you would decide how much time I need to spend there and then come and rescue me from that place.

I do not believe that we humans live again after we die. If I knew that I would live again, I would wait patiently throughout this difficult life. I would know that after I died, things would become different for me.

{After I had been in the place where dead people go for the time you had determined,} you would call for me, and I would answer you. You would be eager to see me, one of the creatures that you had made.
Yes, then you would protect me wherever I went, and you would not be watching to see whether I sinned or not.
You would forgive the things I had done wrong. Yes, it would be as if I had not done them at all.
But just as mountains erode away and rocks tumble down slopes,
just as water wears away stones and floods wash away soil, so you make all people die, even though they hope to keep living.
You make us age the whole time we are living, and then we die. Yes, you make our faces show that we are old and about to die, and then you make us go to the place where dead people go.
When we die, we do not know whether our children will grow up and do things that will cause other people to honor them. If they do shameful things instead, we do not know that either.
When we die, we feel sorry for ourselves, but no one else feels sorry for us. Yes, we grieve for ourselves, but no one else grieves for us.”
Then Eliphaz, Job’s friend from the town of Teman, replied to what Job had said. Eliphaz told him,
“If you were truly wise, you would not have said such useless things. You have said a lot, but it has all been insignificant.
You should not be saying things that do not benefit anyone. No, you should not speak things that are not helpful.
You are actually encouraging others not to respect God. Yes, you are discouraging people from honoring him.
You are wicked, and that is why you say what you do. You are talking in the way that deceptive people talk.
Everything that you say shows that God should punish you. It is not necessary for me to prove that.
{You should not think that you know so much} You were not the first person whom God created. God did not make you when he first formed the world.
You do not listen as God makes his plans. You should not think that you are the only person who is wise.
We know everything that you know. We understand everything that you understand.
My friends and I are saying the same things that old, wise people say, people who were born before your father was.
God wants to comfort you and speak gently to you, but you do not appreciate that.
You should not be allowing yourself to become so emotional. No, you should not be allowing yourself to lose your temper.
You have become angry with God, and so you are saying harsh things against him.
No human being can be sinless. No one on this earth can be completely righteous.
God does not even trust his own angels {to do the right thing every time}. He does not consider the heavens to be completely pure.
So God certainly does not consider people to be pure who commit terrible wrongs, who do evil deeds as often as they drink water.
Job, I want to explain {why you are experiencing so much suffering}. Please listen to me. I have learned many things, and I want to explain them to you.
These are things that wise people have passed down from their ancestors. These wise people have declared all these things openly.
God gave the land {of Edom} exclusively to my wise ancestors. No one came from another country and caused them to think wrongly about God.
Wicked people suffer great pain the whole time that they are alive. God has determined that this will happen constantly to those who oppress others.
Wicked people constantly experience terrible things. They may become wealthy, but they will lose that wealth.
Wicked people lose hope that their troubles will ever end. They are always afraid that they are going to die violently.
They have to go and search for food to eat. They do not know where to find it. They know that they will certainly experience disasters soon.

Wicked people are always afraid that bad things will happen to them. Their fear keeps them from taking actions that might protect them, as if an opposing king had defeated them in a battle {and they had become helpless}.
These things happen to wicked people because they oppose God. They think they are strong enough to defeat Shaddai.
Wicked people stubbornly oppose God as if they had a strong shield to protect themselves against God.
But they are so fat that they would not be able to fight!
Wicked people have to live in cities that others have deserted. They live in homes that others have abandoned. Those homes are about to collapse into a pile of ruins.
Few wicked people become rich, and those who do become rich do not stay rich for very long. No, they do not acquire great wealth.
Wicked people will always be in trouble. They will be like trees whose branches burn up. When God gives the command, they will die.
Wicked people are often foolish and want to get things that are actually worthless. In the end, all they have are those worthless things.
While they are still young, they will die. They are like branches that have broken off a tree and dried up.
Wicked people are like vines whose grapes fall off before they are ripe. They are like olive trees whose blossoms fall off before they produce any fruit.
Surely wicked people will not have any descendants. Those who took money from bribes will not have any money left in the end.
They plan to cause trouble and to do evil things. They continually think of ways to deceive other people.”
Then Job replied to Eliphaz and the others. He said,
“I have heard many things like that before. All of you, instead of helping me, are only causing me to feel more miserable.
I wish that you would stop saying these things that are not helping me. Eliphaz, I do not understand why you feel that you must keep replying to me.
I could say the same things that you are saying if you were the ones suffering instead of me. I could make great speeches to criticize you, and I could shake my head at you {to ridicule you}.
I would think that I was encouraging you by what I said. Yes, I would think that I was relieving you by speaking with you
But as it is, if I talk, I continue to suffer just as much, and if I do not talk, that does not reduce my suffering either.
But now {I will speak to God}. God, you have taken away all my strength, and you have killed all of my children.
You have made me sick, and I have lost a lot of weight, and people think that shows that I am a sinner. They see how thin I am, and they think that proves that I am guilty.

God is so angry with me that he has attacked me and hurt me. Now he is moving his teeth back and forth because he is still so angry with me. He is watching me closely {to see how he can attack me again}.
People look at me with their mouths wide open in order to humiliate me. They hit me in the face because they think I have done wrong. They crowd around me to threaten me.
God has allowed people who do not honor him to mistreat me. He has allowed wicked people to do whatever they want to me.
Previously, I was living peacefully, but then God caused great trouble for me. It is as if he grabbed my neck and shook me to pieces. It is as if he set me up as a target

and people were surrounding me and shooting arrows at me. It is as if those arrows cut open my kidneys and caused the gall from my liver to spill onto the ground. God is not having any mercy on me at all!
It is as if I were a wall that God was breaking down in many places. It is as if God were rushing at me like a soldier who was attacking his enemy.
{I am grieving so deeply that} it is as if I have sewn rough mourning cloth right onto my skin! I feel weak and humiliated.
My face is red because I have cried so much. I have dark circles around my eyes because I have not been sleeping well.
All this has happened to me even though I have not violently harmed anyone and even though I pray sincerely to God.
I feel as if I am the victim of a violent crime, and I want people to show concern about what has happened to me. I do not want anyone to stop me while I am demanding that God act justly toward me.
But even now, I know that there is someone in heaven who will testify for me. He will confirm that what I have done is right.
This person in heaven is my friend, and he will plead with God for me. {At the same time, I will also plead with God so earnestly} that I will weep.
My friend will plead with God for me in heaven the same way one person pleads for another person here on earth.
{I want God to treat me justly now, while there is still time,} because within a few years I will die.
My time to live is almost over. I have no strength left. I am just about to die.
The people who are around me are continually making fun of me. I have to watch them taunt me.
God, even though you would be trying my case, please also guarantee to yourself that I will appear in court and behave as a defendant should. There is certainly no one else who will do that for me.
My friends will not vouch for me, because you have prevented them from understanding that I am innocent. Nevertheless, you will not prove them right by declaring me guilty.

{I know that you will treat me justly because you make sure that people act justly. For example,} you punish people who give false testimony against their neighbors in exchange for a bribe. You make their whole families suffer if they do that.
But because God is punishing me, people use my name to mean someone who was formerly prosperous but who experienced disaster because he was wicked. People even spit in my face {to insult me}.
Because I am very sad, it has become hard for me to see. My whole body has become so thin that it is as if I am not even here.
When people who are truly righteous see what has happened to me, it shocks them. It makes them want to punish people who really disobey God.
Those who are truly righteous will continue to do what is right, and those who are innocent will continue to become stronger.
But as for you friends of mine, we could continue talking, but I do not think that I will conclude that even one of you is wise.
My time to live has almost ended. I have not been able to do the things that I planned to do. I can no longer hope that the things I most desired will happen.

My friends say that the troubles I am experiencing are actually a good thing {because God is using the troubles to correct me}. My friends say that because my troubles have become so bad, that means they must nearly be over.
Suppose the only home I could hope to have was the place where dead people go. Suppose I were going to stay in that dark place.
Suppose I considered the grave to be my family home, and suppose I considered the worms that live in graves to be my family.
Then that would show that I truly do not have good things to hope for. Everyone would recognize that I was not really hoping for anything.
It would be as if everything I hoped for were going to the place where dead people go. Yes, it would be as if people were burying the things I have hoped for with me in a grave.”
Then Bildad, Job’s friend who was a Shuhite, responded to Job. He said,
“Please stop talking! If you would stop talking and listen, we could tell you something.
You seem to think that we are as stupid as cattle.

But by being so angry, you are only hurting yourself. You seem to think that everyone should abandon the earth because life on earth is no longer worth living for anyone after what has happened to you. You seem to think that there should be a great earthquake {as a sign of what an awful thing has happened to you}.
But actually, what has happened to you is not momentous. Wicked people are bound to lose their prosperity. They will not continue to enjoy happiness.
It will be as if the light went out in the tent in which they were living, so that they could not enjoy living there.
Wicked people become weaker {because of the troubles they cause for themselves}. They try to take advantage of other people, but they hurt themselves instead.
Yes, it is as if they walk into a net that they do not realize is there or fall into a pit that someone has concealed as a trap.
It is as if their feet get caught in a trap that does not let them go.
It is as if a loop of rope that someone has hidden on the ground springs up and seizes them when they walk onto it.
Everywhere they go, things cause them to be terrified. It is as if those things are pursuing them and biting at their heels.
They will become weak, as if they did not have enough food to eat. They will always be at risk of disaster.
Diseases will spread all over their skin. Yes, a horrible disease will cause their bodies to decay.
They have a secure life, but it ends suddenly. They die without being able to do anything to save their lives.
Then all of their possessions will belong to other people. Wicked people will have nothing left, as if God had burned up everything they had by making burning stones fall on it.
They will be lifeless, like trees whose roots have dried up and whose branches have all withered.
No one on the earth will remember them anymore. No, no one anywhere in the world will recall what they were like.
Suddenly wicked people will die and no longer be alive. They will no longer be able to live in this world.
They will have no children or grandchildren living in their people group after they die. They will have no descendants living where they previously lived.
Anyone who hears about what happened to them will be shocked.
This is certainly what happens to unrighteous people. Yes, this is what happens to people who do not honor God.”
Then Job replied to Bildad and the others. He said,
“The three of you must stop hurting me and discouraging me by saying that I am wicked!
You have insulted me repeatedly. You should be ashamed for speaking so harshly to me!
Even if it were true that I had done wrong, that would be my concern, not yours!
If you truly think that you are better than I am, and if you are claiming that I must be guilty because I am suffering,
you should realize that it is God who has caused me to suffer. It is as if he had a net and caught me in it, like an animal he wanted to trap.
Listen to me: I protest that God is punishing me unfairly, but no one agrees with me. I cry for help, but no one, not even God, treats me fairly.
It is as if God has blocked my road so that I can not go anywhere. It is as if God has forced me to try to find my way in total darkness.
He has taken away my good reputation. It is as if he has taken a crown of authority off my head.
He is ruining everything that I have. I no longer hope to experience good things in this life. I expect that I will soon die, as if I were a tree that he had pulled completely out of the ground.
He attacks me because he is very angry with me. He treats me as if I were his enemy.
It is as if he were sending an army against me that has surrounded me and is getting ready to destroy me.
God has caused my family to abandon me. Those who know me now act like strangers toward me.
My relatives have left me and my good friends ignore me.
People who were guests in my house and even my female servants act as if they do not recognize me. They treat me like a foreigner whom they do not know.
When I order my servants to come, they do not obey. I have to beg my servants to help me.
My wife stays away from me, even though I was a good father to our children.
Even young children disrespect me. When I stand up to talk, they laugh at me.
All of my intimate friends now detest me. The people I love are hostile to me.
I have become so thin that my bones are visible beneath my skin; I am barely alive.
I plead with you, my three friends, pity me because God is making me suffer greatly.
You should not be making me suffer as well, as if you were God and had to punish sin. You seem to think that you need to keep accusing me of doing things wrong!
I wish that someone would now write what I have been saying in a book {so that people could read it}.
{Or else,} I wish that someone would carve what I have said onto a rock with a chisel and highlight it with lead so that people could always read it.
But I know that there is someone who will defend me and that some day he will appear here on the earth and declare me innocent.
Even after I die and people bury me and my body decays, still, in my body I will see God.
I will see him myself! Yes, I will see him personally! My emotions overwhelm me as I think about that!
But if you three men still think that you need to accuse me of doing wrong because you believe I am responsible for the sufferings I am experiencing,
then you should fear that God will punish you, because God becomes angry with unfair people like you and he punishes them. When that happens, you will know that God punishes people fairly.”
Then Zophar, Job’s friend from the town of Naamah, responded to Job. He said,
“What you have said troubles me greatly, so I want to reply to you right away.
You have insulted me by what you have said. But I have had a good idea about how I should respond to you.
People have known this for a long time, for as long as they have existed:
Wicked people are only briefly successful; people who refuse to honor God are happy only for a short time.
They may seem for a while to be very great and very powerful,
but they will disappear forever like refuse that people throw away. People who knew them will wonder where they have gone.
They will disappear the way a dream ends abruptly when a person wakes up. They will no longer exist. Yes, they will vanish just like the dreams that people have at night.
Those who once saw those wicked people will never see them again. Those wicked people will no longer live where they once lived.
They will have to return the valuable things that they stole from poor people. If they die before they can do that, their children will have to do it.
Wicked people will die before they grow old and others will bury them in the ground.
For wicked people, doing wrong things is like having sweet food in their mouths that they want to continue tasting.
They do not want to stop doing wrong things, as if those things were delicious food that they enjoyed eating.
{But they will regret doing those wrong things.} They will feel like people who eat what they should not eat and get a badly upset stomach that feels as if it is full of poison.
Wicked people try to get as much money as they can but they do not keep it, just as people who eat too much throw up the food that they ate. God makes sure that they lose their wealth.
A person who does evil deeds will die as a result, as certainly as the bite of a poisonous snake kills a person.
A wicked person will not experience the abundant blessings that flow like a stream from God.

Wicked people will have to give back the things that they acquired dishonestly. They will not be able to continue using those things. They will not have the opportunity to enjoy the things they got by doing business,
because they oppressed poor people and refused to help them, and they took other people’s houses by cheating them.
No matter how much they got, they still remained greedy, and as a result, they lost the things that they enjoyed having.
When they finish eating their food, there is never anything left over, because they greedily eat it all. That is why they do not remain wealthy.
While they are still very wealthy, they will suddenly experience trouble. Many people will be hostile to them and hurt them.
Even as wicked people are enjoying luxuries, God will show that he is very angry with them. He will punish them with great suffering, even as they are indulging themselves.
Even as they are trying to escape from smaller punishments, they will experience greater punishments.

It will be as if God had shot an arrow through a wicked person’s body and he had to pull it out of his back. But the shiny point of the arrow would have cut a gash in his liver, and he would know that he was going to die.

God has decided that he will destroy the valuable possessions that wicked people have. It will be as if a fire that God starts will burn them up. Yes, God will destroy every last thing that they have in their homes.

The sins that those wicked people have committed will become apparent. If the sky could speak, it would tell all the wrong things it saw them do. If the earth could speak, it would also be a witness against them.
On the day when God punishes people, he will take away all the possessions of wicked people. It will be as if a flood had washed them away.
That is what God will do to wicked people. That is what God has decreed will happen to them.”
Then Job replied to Zophar and the others. He said,
“Please listen carefully to what I say. That is something that you can do to comfort me.
Be patient with me, and allow me to speak. Then, after I have finished speaking, you can continue to make fun of me if you wish{, although I hope you will not}.
I am not protesting to people about my suffering, I am protesting to God! And so it is certainly acceptable for me to be impatient!
If you consider my situation, it will shock you. That should make you put your hands over your mouths {and say no more}!
When I think about what has happened to me, I am frightened and my entire body shakes.
I do not understand why wicked people live long lives and become very powerful.
They live to see their children grow up and start their own households nearby.
Wicked people live safely in their homes without being afraid. God does not punish them.
Their bulls mate with their cows successfully. Their cows give birth to calves. They do not miscarry.
Wicked people are able to send their young children outside to play {without worrying about what will happen to them}. Their children dance playfully.
The children play tambourines and lyres {as they sing}, and they also play flutes happily.
Wicked people enjoy having good things while they are alive, and then they die peacefully and go to the place where dead people go.
While they are alive, they say to God, ‘Leave us alone; we do not care about how you want us to live our lives!’
Those wicked people also say, ‘It does not matter whether we worship Shaddai. We would not get any advantage by praying to him.’
Wicked people wrongly think that they have become prosperous because of what they have done. I want to think completely differently from the way they think.
It often happens that wicked people die without experiencing any disasters. I do not think that God actually becomes angry with them and punishes them.
God does not destroy them like straw that the wind blows away. It is never as if a whirlwind carries them off.

You say, ‘When people have committed sins, God remembers and punishes their children for those sins.’ I say that God should punish the people who sin, not their children. That way sinners will know that God is punishing them for their own sins.
Wicked people should have the experience of God destroying them. They should know what it is like for Shaddai to punish them in his wrath.
After all, once wicked people die, they are no longer concerned for their families who are still alive.
Since God judges everyone, even those who are in heaven, no one can teach him anything.
Some people die while they are still very healthy. They die when their lives are peaceful and they are not afraid that bad things will happen to them.
Their bodies are fat. Their bones are strong.
Other people are very miserable when they die. They die before good things have happened to them.
Both kinds of people die, and other people bury them. Their bodies all decompose. {Everyone dies, so it is clear that dying is not always the punishment for being wicked.}
Listen, I know what you three are thinking about me. You are wrongly applying to me things that are true about wicked people.
I know you are wrong because you say, ‘God does not allow evil rulers to keep living! God does not allow wicked people to keep living!’

If you want to know what life on earth is really like, you should ask people who travel much {and see many things}. You will have to admit that the things they see and describe show what life is really like.
{Travelers will report} that wicked people do not suffer when there are great disasters. {They will report} that wicked people escape from God’s punishment.
No one dares to accuse wicked people openly of doing wrong. No one punishes them for the evil things they have done.
When wicked people die, others carry their bodies to their graves in a solemn procession. Then people guard their graves to protect them.

It would please wicked people to see how others build mounds over their graves to honor them. It would also please them to see how many people take part in their funeral processions. Many people walk in front of their bodies and many others walk behind them.

Since all of this is true about wicked people, what you have been telling me does not make sense, and it has not comforted me. You have been trying to answer me by telling me things that are not true!”
Then Eliphaz, Job’s friend from the town of Teman, replied to what Job had said. Eliphaz told him,
“No one can do anything to benefit God! No, people can only do things to benefit themselves, and only if they are wise.
It does not give Shaddai any extra pleasure if you live in the way you are supposed to live anyway. It does not make him better off if you improve the way you are living.
God would not be punishing you in this way if you truly honored him. God would not judge you to be guilty for doing that.
No, God must be punishing you because you are very wicked. You must have done a great number of evil things.
You must have unfairly forced poor people to give you things to guarantee that they would pay money back to you. You must have taken the cloaks that they needed to keep them warm.
You must not have given water to people who were thirsty. You must not have given food to people who were hungry.
You must have refused to help others even though you were a wealthy man who owned a lot of land. You must have enjoyed a life of privilege {without being concerned for others}.
When widows came to you for help, you must have sent them away without giving them anything. You must have oppressed orphans.
Because you did all those things, now you are having difficulties in many different areas of your life. Things are happening all of a sudden that scare you.
And so you do not know what to do, as if it had become very dark and you could not see anything. You cannot solve your problems; it is as if you were drowning in a flood of water.
But God lives high up in the heavens. He looks at the earth from a place that is even higher than the stars.
So you should not say, ‘God does not know what people are doing.’ You should not say, ‘Dark clouds keep him from seeing us, so he cannot judge us.’
You should not say, ‘Since he walks on the dome that covers the sky, where there are thick clouds around him, and he can not see what we do.’
You should not continue to conduct your life in the way that evil people have done for many years.
God makes evil people die suddenly while they are still young. They go away completely, as if a flood had swept them away.
Those evil people told God, ‘Leave us alone!’ They also said defiantly, ‘Shaddai can do nothing to harm us!’
Even so, God mercifully gave them many things to enjoy. Nevertheless, I want to think completely differently from the way evil people think.
When good people see that God punishes evil people, they are glad. People who have not done wrong say that those evil people are getting what they deserve.
Those good people say, ‘Now God has destroyed our enemies! It is as if a fire has burned up everything they owned.’
So, Job, I urge you to ask God to forgive you. Restore your relationship with him. If you do that, good things will happen to you.
Do pay attention to what God teaches you. Meditate on what he says.
If you come humbly to Shaddai, he will restore you. {God will certainly do that} if you stop doing the evil things that you have been doing.
Stop trusting in your wealth. It should be as if you are throwing away your gold, even the finest gold you have, onto the dirt and rocks.
If you do that, then Shaddai will be more precious to you than your gold and your silver ever were.
If you do that, then your relationship with Shaddai will make you very happy. You will be able to approach God confidently.
When you pray to God, he will do what you ask him to do. You will have many things to praise God for.
The things that you decide to do will be successful. It will be as if a light were shining on the road in front of you so that you knew just where to walk.
People may cause great difficulties for you. But when you pray and humbly ask God to help you, he will save you.
God will even help people who have done wrong things if you pray for them. God will answer your prayer because you will not have done wrong things.”
Then Job replied to Eliphaz and the others. He said,
“I must still complain about many distressing things. There is much more that I could have protested about.
I wish that I knew where I could find God. {If I knew that,} I would go to the place where he lives.
I would present much evidence to God that I am innocent. I would offer many arguments to prove that.
That way I would know what God would say in reply to everything I would say to him.
He would not use his great power to defeat me. He would listen to me fairly.

I am an honest man, so if I met with God personally, I would be able to discuss things with him reasonably. {If we could do that,} he would declare that I am innocent. After that, he would not punish me again as if I had sinned.
{But I do not know where to find God.} If I went to the east, he would not be there. If I went to the west, I would not see him there.
He makes natural things happen beautifully in the north, but no one there sees him doing those things. He must also go to the south, but no one sees him there either.
Still, he knows how I have conducted my life. When he has finished testing me, he will see that I am as pure as gold whose impurities fire has burned out.
I have lived faithfully in the manner that God wants people to live. I have not stopped living that way.
I have always obeyed the commandments that he has given. I would rather go without food than disobey what God has told us to do.
But God seems to have made up his mind that I am a sinner, and no one can make God change his mind. Whatever he wants to do, he does.
So it seems that God will keep on punishing me until I die. If my present troubles do not kill me, I am sure that God will cause many more troubles for me!
So the thought of coming into his presence greatly frightens me. When I think about what he can do, that makes me very afraid of him.
I am afraid because I am no longer brave after what God has done to me. Shaddai has made me very frightened.
I have lived to experience terrible things, and that is why I am so frightened. I can only imagine that the future will be just as bad as the present.
Shaddai should set times when he judges evil people. The people who obey God never seem to see him judge evil people.
Some evil people remove boundary markers so that they can steal other people’s land. Some evil people steal other people’s sheep and put them in with their own sheep.

Some evil people take away donkeys that belong to children who have no fathers to protect them. They make loans to widows, and then they take oxen that belong to them to guarantee that the widows will pay back the money. {But without the oxen, the widows cannot grow crops, so they cannot repay the loans, and the evil people keep the oxen.}
Poor people do not want evil people to know where they are, so they do not walk on the main roads. Poor people stay in hiding places in order to avoid evil people.
In fact, poor people have to search in the desert plain for food to feed their children, as if they were wild donkeys.
The poor people pick up leftover grain in other people’s fields. They gather leftover grapes from vineyards that evil people own.
During the night they do not have thick garments to cover their bodies, so they are not able to stay warm.
{Poor people have no homes, so} when rain showers come from the mountains, they get very wet. They have to huddle under rock ledges to shelter themselves from the rain.
Some evil people even take babies away from their mothers while they are nursing! They take the babies as a guarantee that their mothers will repay money that they have lent them.
Poor people do not have adequate clothing. They also do not have adequate food, even though they carry around bundles of grain because they work to bring in other people’s harvests.

Evil people hire poor people to make oil from olives that grow on olive trees on their property. The evil people also hire poor people to tread on grapes that grow on their vines to make juice for wine. But they do not allow the poor people to drink any of the wine when they are thirsty.
In the cities, poor people groan because they are suffering. People whom evil people have wounded cry out to God for help. But God does not seem to care about what the evil people are doing to them.
These evil people are like others who do not obey God. They do not try to understand what God wants or to do it.
Murderers go out in the dim light of morning so they can kill vulnerable people {without being caught}. They are like thieves who steal things in the dark of night {in order to avoid being caught}.
Men who want to commit adultery watch for evening to come. They say, ‘I am going to make sure that no one recognizes me,’ and they disguise themselves.
During the night, robbers find ways to get into other people’s houses and steal things. But during the day, they stay in their own homes. They do not like being out where it is light.

These evil people all stay at home during the day because morning is as scary for them as the dark of night is for other people. They stay up at night because they like being awake at night when things happen that terrify others.
However, those wicked people will not live long lives. God will keep anything from growing on the land that they own. No one will go and work in their vineyards.
Just as water from melting snow dries up when it is hot and there is no rain, those evil people will go to the place where dead people go.
When they die, maggots will eat their corpses, and no one will remember them. Even their mothers will forget about them! Those wicked people will be like trees that fall down and rot.
Those evil people mistreat women who do not have children to care for them. Those evil people never help widows.

But God, by his power, gets rid of people who hurt others because they are stronger than those others. When it is clear that God is going to punish those evil people, they know that they are going to die.
God allows them to think that they are secure, and so they do not worry, but God is carefully watching how they live.

Those evil people may prosper for a little while, but suddenly they will be gone. God will show that they were not greater than others. God will make them die like all other people. Then they will be like stalks of grain that farmers have cut off.
What I have said is certainly true. Now that I have explained it, there is no one who can show that I am a liar and prove me wrong.”
Then Bildad, Job’s friend who was a Shuhite, responded to Job. He said,
