“God is very powerful. Everyone should honor him greatly. God causes everything to be orderly high up in heaven.
No one can count all the stars in the sky. When the sun rises, it shines on everyone.
Since God is so great, no person can be righteous compared with him. No human being is innocent by his standards.
Consider this: God is so glorious that he does not even consider the full moon to be bright! Even the white light of the stars does not seem pure to him.
So God would certainly not consider mortal humans to be pure!”
Then Job replied to Bildad and the others. He said,
“I am struggling, but you have not really helped me. I am not able to overcome my difficulties, but you have not rescued me.
I need good advice, but you have not given me any. You have said many things, but they have not been helpful.
I suppose you think that God helped you tell me important things. But God was not really speaking through you.
{Let me tell you how great God really is.} The spirits of dead people tremble with fear at God. They are deep in the earth, below the waters where the sea creatures live.
God knows all about those who are in the place where dead people go. Nothing prevents God from seeing what is there.
God created the dome of the sky to make an orderly world. God created the dry land where previously there was nowhere for people to live.
God uses clouds as containers for rainwater, and he prevents that water from bursting the clouds.
God can make clouds so thick that even the bright moon cannot shine through them.
God has set the horizon in place as the outer edge of the oceans. The horizon is at the place where the sky meets the earth.
Sometimes even the mountains that hold up the sky shake, as if God were scolding them and they were afraid.
God used his power to restrain the oceans; by his skill he destroyed Rahab, the huge sea monster.
God can make the sky clear by blowing away the clouds. {God brings order everywhere in creation} by overcoming the forces of chaos.

But I have described only a little bit of what God does. It is as if we can only hear someone whisper about him. When we hear mighty thunder, we realize that God is far too great for us to understand.”
Job kept speaking to his three friends. He said,
“I will promise you something as surely as God exists, even though he has treated me unfairly. I will promise you something as surely as Shaddai exists, even though he has made my life so unpleasant.
I will insist on it for as long as I am alive. Yes, for as long as I am still breathing, I will insist on it.
I promise that I will not say the wrong thing! I promise that I will not say anything to deceive anyone!
And so I will never say that what you three have said about me is true. Until the day that I die, I will insist that I have been living as God wants people to live.
I will insist that I am innocent. I will never say anything different. That way, for as long as I live, I will not feel badly about saying something that was not true.
I want to be just the opposite of an evil person. I want to disagree with the way anyone who is a bad person is living.
I want to be the opposite of an evil person because when God decides it is time for that person to die, he can only expect that God will then punish him for the wrong things that he has done.
When evil people are in trouble, God does not rescue them when they pray for help.
Evil people are not happy about what Shaddai does. They do not speak with God in prayer in good times as well as in bad times.
I need to teach you three something about how God actually deals with the people of this world.
You three have certainly seen for yourselves how God treats people. So you should not have been telling me things that have made so little sense.
I will tell you how God punishes evil people. This is what Shaddai does to those who mistreat others:
Even if they have many children, those children will die in wars, or they will die because they do not have enough food to eat.
Any children who are still alive after their evil parents die will perish from diseases. Not even the wife of an evil man will mourn for him if he dies.
Sometimes evil people accumulate a large amount of money and they acquire many valuable articles of clothing.
But even if evil people become rich, they will die, and then righteous people will get their clothes. Honest people will get their money and share it with one another.
The houses that they build are as weak as spider webs. Their houses are flimsy, like the huts that watchmen live in while they guard people’s fields.
God makes evil people lose their money. It is as if they are rich when they go to bed one night, but the next morning they wake up to find that their money is all gone.

When evil people realize that God is punishing them, they become very afraid, as if those fears were water in which they were drowning. God soon destroys the evil people, as if a whirlwind carried them away in the night.
It is as if a windstorm from the desert picks them up and carries them away from their homes. No one ever sees them again.
It is as if a wind like that blows steadily against them while they are running away, trying to escape from its force.
It is as if such a wind were clapping its hands at them to mock them. It is as if such a wind blew them out of their houses and stayed there laughing at them.
There certainly are places where people dig to find silver. There certainly are places where people refine gold that they have dug from the ground.
People get iron from ore that they dig out of the ground. They get copper by heating and melting ore that contains it.
People use lamps so that they can see while they work far down under the ground. They search for ore in many places where it is very dark.

People dig shafts deep into the ground in places that are far from where other people live, As they work underground, the people who walk above them are not aware of them. People have to climb down ropes in order to descend into the deep shafts they have dug.
Food grows on the surface of the ground. But deep below the ground, miners make fires to break apart the rocks.
The stones that people dig from under the ground contain sapphires. The dirt they dig up contains bits of gold.
Even birds that have very good eyesight can not see deep down into these mines. Even birds such as falcons have not looked into them.
Strong beasts can go wherever they want, but they have never gone to those places. Not even lions have gone there.
Miners dig through even very hard rock. It is as though they are turning mountains upside down in order to get at the ore that is at the bases of them.
Miners cut tunnels through rocks in order to find many precious things.
They dam up small streams to stop the water from flowing. That allows them to find things that were hidden beneath the water of the streams.
{It takes great effort to find valuable ore.} It is even more difficult to obtain wisdom. Yes, it is very difficult to obtain understanding.
Humans do not know how to obtain wisdom. Wisdom is not available on earth, where people live.
It is as though the ocean depths and the water of the seas said, ‘There is no wisdom here!’
People can not buy wisdom by paying for it with gold or silver.
Wisdom is worth much more than fine gold that comes from the land of Ophir. {Wisdom is worth much more} than very valuable stones.
Wisdom is worth much more than gold or beautiful quartz. It is more expensive than an article made of pure gold.
Wisdom is worth more than coral or jasper. The price of wisdom is higher than the price of rubies.
Wisdom is worth more than topaz from the land of Cush. One can not express the value of wisdom even in terms of gold.
So, then, wisdom is very difficult to obtain; understanding is indeed a very valuable thing to get.
Living creatures are not able to see it. Not even the birds can see it while they are up in the sky.
Even after people die, they do not have a better experience of wisdom in the different place to which they go.
God is the only one who knows how people can become wise.
God knows this because he can see everything on earth, even in its most remote places. God can see everything that is below the sky.
He decided how strongly the winds should blow and how much rain should be in the clouds.
God decided where rain should fall and what path lightning should take from the clouds down to the ground.
At that time, he identified wisdom and recognized that it was very valuable. He was delighted by its capabilities and made it a permanent part of his creation.

Then God told human beings, ‘Listen! You will become wise to the extent that you respect me. If you want to understand what you should do, you must first decide that you will not do anything wicked.’”
Job kept speaking to his three friends. He said,
“I wish that I could be as I was previously during the time when God was taking care of me.
During that time, it was if God was shining a light on me so that I could see where I was going even in the darkness.
At that time I was young and strong. Because God was my friend, he protected where I lived.
Shaddai was still present with me during that time when all my children were still alive and living near me.
My herds provided me with plenty of milk. My olive trees provided me with plenty of oil.
I used to go to the place where the elders gathered at the city gate. The people had reserved a seat for me there, and I would sit in it.
When young men saw me, they stepped aside respectfully. When older men saw me, they stood up respectfully.
The leaders of the people used to stop talking when I arrived. They made sure they did not say anything{, because they knew it would not be as good as what I was going to say}.
Even the most important leaders became quiet. It was as if they were not even able to speak.
When people heard what I had to say, they said good things about me. They recognized that I had given wise counsel, and they approved of me
{They approved of me} because I had helped those who were poor and who were calling for help. {They also approved of me because} I aided orphans who had no fathers to help them.
People who had been suffering and were about to die praised me {for rescuing them}. I made widows very happy by helping them.
It was in my character to make sure that I and others did what was right. Yes, it was in my character to make sure that people treated one another in a way that was just.
I helped people who could not see, as if I were seeing for them. I helped people who could not walk, as if I were walking for them.
I protected poor people the way a father protects his children. In the courts, I defended even people who were strangers to me.
I made wicked people stop oppressing others. It was as if I were breaking the jaws of a wild animal to make it drop its victim from its teeth.
At that time I thought, ‘I am certainly going to live a long life, and then I will die at home with my family.
I am like a tree whose roots reach down into the water and whose branches become wet with dew each night.
People continually honor me, and I stay strong like a new bow.’
When I spoke, people waited to hear what I would say. They remained silent until I advised them what they should do.
After I finished speaking, they did not say anything, because what I had said was so satisfying.
They were as eager to hear me speak as farmers are for it to rain. They listened to me with great appreciation, just as the ground seems to welcome the rain that falls in the spring.
I helped people who felt discouraged. I remained cheerful even as I helped them deal with difficult situations.

As their leader, I decided what things would be good for them to do. They respected me, just as soldiers respect the king who commands their army. I was kind and sympathetic, like someone who comforts people who are mourning.
But now, men who are younger than I am make fun of me. They are men whose fathers I would not even have hired to help my dogs guard my sheep!
And I would not hire any of those young men to work for me either. They are already feeble.
{No one hires them,} so they are poor and go hungry and have become thin. They have to eat roots that they find in places where no crops have grown for a long time.
They look among bushes to find leaves that they can eat. They pull up broom trees and eat their roots.
{When they come near villages,} people shout at them, as they would at a thief, to make them leave their area.
They have to live in riverbeds, in holes in the ground, and in caves on the sides of cliffs.
{During the day} they huddle under thorn bushes. There they howl like animals because they are so hungry.
They are people without good sense, and they have never achieved anything significant. People force them to leave their towns.
But these despicable young men sing songs to make fun of me! If they think God is punishing someone for being a sinner, they call that person ‘another Job.’
They hate me and they stay away from me, but if we happen to meet, they spit right in my face.
I am not able to defend myself against these young men, because God has taken away my strength. He has humiliated me. So they can do whatever they want to me.
Gangs of these young men threaten me. They shove me aside when they pass by. They think of new ways to hurt me.
I am not able to escape from them, even as they keep doing worse things to me. No one else would do the things they do to me.
It is as if I were a city and they were an army that had broken through its wall and sent in waves of troops to destroy the city.
I am afraid of many things. I have no dignity left, and I do not expect that I will ever get out of this situation.
I feel as if I am about to die, but in the meantime, I am suffering greatly.
My body aches during the night. I feel pain continually.
I have such a serious disease that my skin no longer looks the same. It seems as if I will always be sick.
God has made me suffer so much that I have been sitting here on the ground. I am even beginning to look like the dust and ashes in which I have been sitting.
Even though I pray to you, God, you do not respond. I try to get your attention, but you do not do anything to help me.
You used to be kind to me, but you are not kind to me anymore. You are using your mighty power to make me suffer.
It is as if you have sent a great wind to pick me up and carry me away. It is as if you are making a violent storm blow me around.
Certainly I know that you are going to make me die. That is what happens to everyone who ever lives.
However, when someone falls down, he certainly reaches out with his hand for help. When someone is in trouble, he certainly calls for help.
{So it is appropriate for me to ask for your help now, God.} After all, I wept for people myself when they were experiencing troubles. I felt sorry for poor people.
I am asking for help because although I expected good things to happen to me, evil things happened instead. It was as if I was waiting for dawn but another night started instead of a new day.
I am very distressed all the time. I suffer during every day.
I look as if I have to work outside all day to make a living. I humble myself by pleading openly for people to help me.
{No one wants to come near me.} It is as if I am a jackal or ostrich living out in the wilderness.
My skin has become dark, and it is peeling off. I have a fever that causes my body to feel as if it were burning up.
Previously, if you came to my house, you would hear musical instruments playing happy songs. If you came now, you would only hear people crying and singing sad songs.
I have made a solemn promise to myself that I will not look at a woman in a lustful way. So I would not look at a woman who was not my wife and want to have sexual relations with her.
{If I did not do what I promised,} God who is in heaven would certainly punish me. Shaddai in heaven would make sure that I got what I deserved.
{I would not have done wrong in that way, because I know that} unrighteous people experience calamities. People who do what is wrong experience disasters {when God punishes them}.
I know that God sees everything that I do. He is aware of each individual action that I take.
I solemnly declare that I have not lied to others and that I have not tried to deceive others.
I only ask God to judge me fairly. If he does that, he will find that I am innocent.
I solemnly declare that I have continually acted properly. I have not seen wrong things to do and then done them. I am not guilty of committing sin.
If I have been lustful or deceptive, I hope that when I plant seeds, someone else will harvest the crops and eat them. Or may someone uproot the crops that are growing in my fields!
I solemnly declare that I have not been attracted to another man’s wife. I have not made secret arrangements with a woman to have sexual relations with her while her husband was away.
If I have done that, I hope that my own wife will be attracted to another man and that she will have sexual relations with him.
If I had sexual relations with another man’s wife, that would be a terrible sin. If I were caught and her husband brought me to court, the judges would certainly decide to punish me.

{I would have to pay a fine that would cost me everything I owned.} It would be as if a fire had burned everything I had right to the ground. It would be as if someone pulled out all the crops that were growing in my fields.
I solemnly declare that when my male or female servants complained to me about something, I took their complaint seriously and made sure that I treated them fairly.

I knew that if I did not treat my servants fairly, I could not expect God to be merciful to me when he judged me. If God came to help my servants, I could offer no excuse for the way I had treated them.
{I am no different from my servants, so I have no right to mistreat them.} The same God created each one of us.

I solemnly declare that from the time that I was young, I have taken care of orphans and I have protected widows. I have not failed to provide poor people with the things that they needed. I have not caused widows to lose hope. I have not eaten all of my food by myself and not shared it with orphans.
I solemnly declare that I provided clothes for poor people when I saw that they were suffering from lack of clothing. I have provided warm outer garments for needy people.
I gave them warm clothes that my servants had woven from the wool of my sheep. The poor people thanked me for helping them.

I solemnly declare that I never threatened an orphan who brought a case against me in the public square. Even if I knew that the other elders would favor me, I made sure that the orphan received fair treatment.
If I have neglected poor people or oppressed orphans, may the arm {that I did not use to help them but used instead to threaten them} fall right out of its socket!
I have not done wrong things such as I have been describing, because I respect God and I know that he punishes sin. I would not sin against such a majestic God!
I solemnly declare that I have not depended on wealth as a source of security and power.
I solemnly declare that I did not think that I was better than other people because I had many possessions and because I had become very rich.
I solemnly declare that I never looked at the sun when it was shining or at the beautiful moon
and made a gesture to worship them. I never wanted to do that.

If I had worshiped the sun or the moon and people found out that I had, the judges would certainly decide to punish me for that too, because I would have been worshiping a false god instead of the true God.

I solemnly declare that I have not been glad when my enemies have suffered misfortunes. I have not thought that I was better than they were when they experienced disasters. I have not sinned by praying that God would curse people who hated me and cause them to die.
I solemnly declare that I have invited travelers to stay in my house. Visitors have not had to sleep in the streets. My servants talk about how I give food to anyone who needs it.
I know that people generally try to hide their sins. But I solemnly declare that I have not done that.
I did not let fear of what people would say about me or think of me keep me from admitting that I had done wrong and making amends.

I wish that I had someone who would judge my case against God! I hereby declare that all that I have just said is true. Now I wish that Shaddai would state his case. I would like to see his written statement of charges against me.
If Shaddai wrote out his charges against me, I would not be ashamed, because I know that I am innocent. I would display the charges publicly{, because they would actually list what I had not done}.
I would explain to God in detail how I was innocent of each charge. I would approach him as a ruler would: without being afraid.
I solemnly declare that I have not defrauded the people who farm my land. They have no reason to cry out for justice against me.

I solemnly declare that I have taken only a fair share of the crops that people have grown on my land. I have made sure that the people who grew crops on my land kept enough of them to feed their families.

If I have cheated the people who farm my land, then I wish that thorns would grow in my fields instead of wheat. I wish that bad weeds would grow there instead of barley!” After this, Job said nothing further to defend himself to his three friends.
Then Job’s three friends stopped replying to him, because Job was confident that he was innocent.

Then a man named Elihu{, who had been listening as Job spoke with his friends,} became very angry with Job. Elihu was the son of Barakel. He was a Buzite and he belonged to the clan of Ram. He became angry because Job continued to claim that he was innocent and that God had been wrong to punish him.

Elihu also became angry with Job’s three friends. He became angry because they had insisted that Job must have done many things that were wrong, but they had not been able to prove any of their accusations.
Now Elihu was much younger than Job’s three friends. That was why he had let them speak to Job first.
But when Elihu realized that the three men had nothing more to say to Job, he became very angry.
This is what Elihu said. (He was the son of Barakel. He was a Buzite.) “I am young, and you all are much older than I am. So I was hesitant. I was afraid to tell you what I was thinking.
I said to myself, ‘I should let the people who are older speak. Older people should be able to explain how to understand things wisely.’
However, even as I was saying that, I felt the Spirit of God stirring within me. Yes, I felt Shaddai inspiring me so that I could understand.
Humble people can also be wise. Younger people can also recognize the right thing to do.
So now I want to ask you, ‘Please listen to me. Let me too say what I have been thinking.’
Now I let the three of you speak first. I waited while you thought carefully about what you should say, and I listened to your arguments.
I paid careful attention to what you were saying. But in the end, none of you was able to prove that what Job said was wrong. None of you could respond to his arguments.
So do not tell yourselves, ‘We have discovered what is wise!’ It is God who must show Job that he is wrong. Someone relying on human thinking will not be able to do that.
You were angry with Job, and so you have not answered him well. But Job has said nothing to make me angry, so I will not answer him the way you have.
The three of you are just sitting there in a daze, not saying anything more, because you cannot think of what to say to Job.
And since you are not speaking, since you have stopped answering Job, I do not feel that I need to wait any longer before speaking to Job myself.
So now I too will respond to Job. I will share my view of his situation.
I must speak, because I have plenty to say, and something inside me is forcing me to say it.
I feel as if I am a container of wine that is stretching more and more and that will soon burst because of the fermentation.
I must speak, and then I will be able to rest from the effort of restraining myself from speaking. So I will now say something in reply to all of you.
I will not favor either Job or you his friends. I will not try to flatter anyone.
Indeed, I have not gotten into the habit of flattering people, because I believe that if I did that, God would quickly destroy me.
So now, Job, I ask you to listen carefully to everything that I am going to say.
I am ready to speak to you and tell you what I think.
What I say will express my sincere feelings of concern for you. I will only tell you what is genuinely true.
You can trust me as someone whom God’s Spirit created. You can trust me as someone whom Shaddai made alive.
{Once I have spoken,} respond to me if you can. Think carefully about how you will reply to me.
Now you wanted God to answer you, and I will do that for him. But I am human, just like you,
so you do not need to be afraid of me. I will not speak to you harshly.
I listened carefully to you as you spoke, and this is what I heard you say:
‘I am righteous. I have not committed any sins. I am innocent. I have not done things that are wrong.
Nevertheless, God looks for excuses to punish me. He treats me as if I were his enemy.
He judges me by very strict standards. He closely observes everything that I do.’
However, what you have said is incorrect. I will explain why. {You do not realize what God is actually doing, since} it is beyond human understanding.
You should not be protesting that God does not respond to what anyone says.
God actually does speak to people in various ways. People just do not realize how he is doing that.
Sometimes God speaks to people at night in dreams and visions when they are sound asleep in bed.
God reveals things to people at those times. He shows them that they need to change the way that they have been living.
God speaks in that way to get people to stop doing evil deeds. God wants to prevent people from sinning because they have become proud.
In this way, God prevents people from dying. Otherwise, someone might kill them violently.
God also corrects people by making them so ill that they have to lie in bed. They feel constant agony in their bodies.
They feel so sick that they do not want to eat anything, not even their favorite foods.
They lose so much weight that there appears to be no flesh between their skin and their bones.
They become so sick that they are about to die. The angels who cause people to die start coming to get them.
However, sometimes a special kind of angel may come to a person and tell him on behalf of God how he can change the way that he has been living so that he will not die.

{If the person changes the way that he has been living,} then God will forgive him. God will tell the angels who cause people to die, ‘Do not cause this person to die! I can see that I should allow him to live, because now he will do what is right.’
When that happens, the person will become healthy again and his skin will appear as fresh as the skin of a child. He will be as strong again as he was when he was young.
Then God will once again treat him as a righteous person. He will pray to God, and God will answer his prayer. He will come into God’s presence joyfully.
He will sing a song of thanksgiving and tell the people who are listening, ‘I sinned; yes, I did things that were not right, but God did not punish me in the way that I deserved.
He has saved me from going to the place where dead people are. And so I will continue to enjoy being alive!’
Indeed, God does this for many people.
He keeps them from going to the place where dead people are. That way they can continue to enjoy being alive.
So Job, please listen to me. Do not say anything right now; just allow me to speak.
{After I have spoken, then} if you have something more that you want to say to me, say it, because I would like to show that you are innocent.
However, if you have nothing more that you want to say, then just listen to me. I will explain to you how you can understand your situation in a wise way.”
Then Elihu continued to speak, and he said,
“I want everyone who is wise to hear what I am about to say. I want everyone who knows a lot to listen to me.

I want you to listen carefully to me because when people hear others speak, they need to decide whether what the others are saying is right or wrong. They do this just as people taste food to decide whether it is good or bad.
I would like all of us to decide together who is right, Job or his friends. I would like us to find out together what is a good way to understand his situation.
We need to consider this carefully together because Job has said, ‘I am innocent, but God has not judged me fairly.’
Job has said he would not lie about whether he has done what is right. He has spoken as if God had shot him with an arrow and wounded him so badly that he will die, even though he is innocent.
I have not heard anyone else speak the way Job does. People drink water to satisfy their thirst, and mocking God seems to satisfy Job.
His friends are people who do what is wrong. He spends time with wicked people.
We know that this is true about him because he has said, ‘It is useless for people to want to please God.’
So, all of you who understand things well, listen to me! God would never consider doing anything that was wicked! No, Shaddai would never consider doing anything that was wrong!

We can be confident that God treats people fairly because we can see that he rewards or punishes people properly for what they have done. God gives people what they deserve for the manner in which they have lived.
No, God never does anything wicked. Shaddai always treats people fairly.
God did not need anyone to give him the authority to rule the people who live on the earth. He did not need anyone to put him in control of all the people in the world.
If God ever thought only about himself and not also about the world he created, if God ever stopped keeping people and animals alive,
then every living thing would die immediately, and the bodies of people would soon become soil again.
So, Job, if you truly want to understand, then listen carefully to what I am about to say.
God could certainly not hate what is right and still rule the world. So you really cannot say that God, who is righteous and powerful, has done something wrong.
God tells some kings that they are worthless, and he says to some officials that they are wicked.
God does not treat rulers better than he treats other people. God does not treat rich people more respectfully than he treats poor people. After all, God created all people.
If people use their power to oppress others, God punishes them by killing them. Those people are not expecting to have troubles and die, and humans do not kill them, but God kills them very quickly.
God punishes oppressive people because he sees everything that people do. God is aware of each individual action that a person does.
Wicked people can not escape from God by hiding in places where it is very dark.
Now God does not need to examine a person further before passing judgment on that person.
God does not need to investigate what people have done. He knows whether important people have done wrong, and he destroys them if they have. He then appoints others to take their places.
Because he already knows what they have done, he removes them quickly and gets rid of them.
God kills them because of the wicked things that they have done. Many people see him do it.
God kills them because they stopped doing what he wanted them to do and did not pay attention to his commands.
They mistreated poor people. Those poor people prayed to God for help, and God answered their prayers.

Yet even if God decides not to punish wicked people right away, no one can criticize him. If God does not reveal what he is doing, no one can understand it. God controls every nation and every person.
God makes sure that those who rule honor him. He makes sure that rulers do not oppress the people whom they rule.
Suppose someone says to God, ‘I recognize that I am suffering because I have sinned. I do not want to sin any longer.
Please show me what sins I have committed. I will stop doing anything that is evil.’

If a person said that to God, do you think that God would continue to punish him? Now you have been saying that God does not treat people fairly, so it is important for you to decide what you think God would do. I will not suggest the answer myself. We would like to hear you say what you think about this.
{But unfortunately, I believe that} when people who have good sense and people who are wise hear my question and your answer, they will say to me,
‘Job is speaking ignorantly. What he says does not make sense.’
It would be good if God put Job on trial and investigated every last detail of his case. God should do that because Job has been speaking just as wicked people speak.

God should put Job on trial because in addition to sinning, he is saying that God does not treat people fairly. Knowing that we were watching, he clapped his hands to insult God. He has made long speeches to say that God has punished him unjustly.”
Then Elihu continued to speak, and he said,
“Job, it is not right for you to say that you have been doing what is right but God has been doing what is wrong.
You are basically saying that when you ask, ‘What good things have I received because I have not sinned? How am I better off than I would be if I had sinned?’
I will answer those questions for you, and I will also respond to what your three friends have said.
Job, look up at the sky. See how high the clouds are above you! {God is far higher than that!}
So if you sin, that does not harm God at all. Even if you do many wrong things, that does not hurt him.
On the other hand, if you do what is right, that does not make God better off. No, you are not giving God something that he does not already have.
The only ones who suffer if you are wicked are other people. The only ones you might help by being good are other humans.
People call for others to help them because of the many things that wicked people do that make them suffer. They call for help because of the things that powerful people do to oppress them.
But people do not ask God, their Creator, to help them. People do not expect God to enable them to sing joyful songs because he has rescued them.
People do not realize that God wants to teach them how to live wisely. God does that for people, not for wild animals or for the birds in the sky.
Even when people do pray to God for help, God does not answer them, because they arrogantly continue to do what is wrong.
God, the Almighty One, does not respond at all when people pray but do not really mean what they are saying.

You are telling God that you have made your case against him but that you are still waiting for him to answer your accusations. You are saying that God has not been helping you. Since you say those things, you should certainly not expect God to respond to you!
You also say that God does not pay much attention when people commit sins, and so he does not become angry and punish them.
My friends, you see that Job has said things that are completely useless. He says many things without knowing what he is talking about.”
Then Elihu said some more things to Job:
“Job, be patient with me a little longer as I explain things to you. Be patient, because I have more to say in order to show that God does not do anything wrong.
I will tell you what I have learned from many sources. I will show that God, who made me, always does what is right.
You can indeed listen patiently because I will not say anything to you that is false. I am here with you as someone who understands things well.
Truly, God is very powerful, but he values every person. He understands everything completely.
He does not allow wicked people to remain alive, but he helps people whom others have been oppressing.
He always protects people who are righteous. He makes them prosper as if they were kings, and he causes others to honor them continually.
Sometimes people suffer great troubles because they have done wrong things.
When they do, God shows them what they have done wrong. He shows them that they committed these sins because they were proud.
He enables them to understand what he is teaching them. He commands them to stop sinning.
If they obey him and once again live as he wishes, they will prosper and be happy for as long as they live.
But if they do not obey him, they will die violently because they did not seek to understand how God wanted them to live.
People who do not respect God continue to be angry with God. They do not ask God to help them even when they are suffering because of their sins.
They can only make a living in a dishonorable way, and they die while they are still young.
God actually uses suffering to keep people from perishing because of their sins. By making them suffer, he causes them to listen to what he is telling them.
Job, I believe that God wants to bring you out of your troubles and allow you to live without distress. He wants you to be happy and prosperous.
However, you are still saying bad things about God the way a wicked person would. That is why God is punishing you so severely.
You are angry with God, but do not let that lead you to say disrespectful things about God. If you did that, God would not accept even a very large bribe to pardon you.
God would not want your money and so pardon you. He would not take gold or a great deal of money as a bribe.
You should not wish that you could die so that your suffering would be over. Once people die, they are gone.
Be careful not to commit sin. It seems that you would rather defy God than learn what he wants to teach you through suffering.
Truly, God is so powerful that he can do great things. He is better than any other teacher.
No one has ever told him what he should do. No one has ever had to tell him that what he was doing was wrong.
People have often sung songs to praise him. You too should remember what he has done and praise him for it.
Everyone has seen what God has done, but even so, people only understand it a little.
How great God is! We are not able to understand how great he is, and we are not able to determine how old he is.
Indeed, God draws water up from the earth and puts it in clouds and causes it to become rain.
This rain pours down from the clouds and abundant showers fall on the earth, where people live.
No one can really understand how the clouds spread across the sky or how it thunders in the sky where God lives.
See how God causes lightning to flash all around him! The lightning is so bright that it lights up even the deep ocean.
Because his storms are so great, God uses them to punish wicked people. But he also uses the rain from these storms to provide abundant food for righteous people.
It is as if God picks up lightning in his hands and sends it to strike where he wants it to.
God makes thunder to announce that there will be a storm. We also know that a storm is coming when we hear cattle making extra noise.
My heart really pounds when I think about that! I feel as if it is jumping around inside me.
Listen, all of you, to the thunder! It is as if God is roaring!
God makes such loud thunder that people can hear it throughout the land. God makes such bright lighting that people can see it from far away.
After lightning flashes, we hear thunder, which sounds like God speaking very loudly. Then, after the thunder, God makes more lightning.
When we hear thunder, it is as if God is shouting in an amazing way. God does things that are too wonderful for us to understand.
For example, God can cause snow to cover the ground, and when he tells a rain shower to rain even harder, it becomes a downpour.
When God makes it rain so hard, everyone has to stop working outside. This shows all people, whom he has made, what great things he is able to do.
When it rains, the animals go into their hiding places and they stay there until the rain stops.
Storms come from the place where they start, and cold winds come from the north.
In the winter, cold winds turn water into ice. The water in lakes freezes solid.
God truly fills the clouds with water droplets. He makes lightning flash from many clouds.
He causes the clouds to move around over the places where people live so that they can accomplish everything that he wants them to do.

God may send storms to punish people. God may send storms to water the land that he made. God may send storms to help people by providing rain to make their crops grow. God makes all of these things happen.
Job, listen to what I am saying. Just think about the wonderful things that God does.
Are you able to explain how God arranges the clouds in the sky and makes lightning flash down from them?
Are you able to explain how God is able to make clouds float in the sky? Can you understand all of the wonderful things that God does? God understands everything completely!
Are you able to explain how God can bring in stifling air from the desert and make it so hot that you cannot stay cool if you wear clothes?
Are you able to explain how God made the sky so that it would stay firmly in place above the earth?
I doubt that you could tell us what to say to God. People do not know enough to be able to defend themselves if they spoke with God.
I would not dare tell God that I needed to speak with him! If I did that, then he might destroy me!
You know that people can not look directly at the sun when it shines brightly in the sky after the wind has blown the clouds away.
When God appears, he has glittering light all around him. His glory is so bright that it makes us afraid. {So if we cannot even look at the sun, how could we look at God?}
Shaddai has very great power, and we do not know how to get near to him. He always acts righteously, and he never mistreats anyone.
That is why everyone should have great respect for him. Any people who think that they are wise do not impress him.”
Then Yahweh spoke to Job from inside the storm that had been approaching. He said to him,
“You have been speaking ignorantly, and as a result, you have been making it harder for people to understand my actions.
I am going to ask you some questions, so get ready to answer them directly.
Where were you when I began to create the earth? Since you claim to know so much, tell me how I did that.
Who decided how large the earth would be? Who made sure that it was the right size? If you know as much as you claim, you ought to be able to tell me that.

What keeps the earth from collapsing? Who made sure that everything on the earth would be in the right position? The earth was so beautiful when I made it that it was as if the first stars all sang a song to celebrate it. All of the angels gave a great cheer when they saw the earth.
When I made the land, the sea could have flowed over it. Who prevented the sea from flooding the earth?
Now the clouds in the sky float over the sea as if they were its clothing. Night and day happen at sea just as they do on land.
I decided how much of the area under the sky the sea would cover. I made barriers at the shore of the sea to keep it off the land.
I proclaimed that the sea could only come up so far on the shore and not come any farther. I said that its great waves could only flow up to a certain place on the land.
Job, have you ever commanded a day to begin? Have you told the sun where it needed to rise on a certain day?
When day comes, wicked people all around the world stop doing the bad things they do at night when no one can see them.
In the light of day, people can see the hills and valleys on earth clearly. The earth seems to take shape the way clay takes shape when people press a seal onto it or the way folds form in clothing.
When daylight comes, wicked people do not have the darkness that they like. They are no longer able to hurt other people.
Job, have you traveled to the springs at the bottom of the sea? Have you gone and seen what is at the very bottom of the oceans?
Has someone shown you how to get to the place where dead people are? Do you know where the entrance to that dark place is?
Do you know how big the earth is? Tell me, if you know all these things!
Do you know how to get to the place where light comes from? Do you know where darkness comes from?
Would you know how to get to those places so that you could bring light and darkness to them?
If you had been alive when I created the world, then you would know the answers to these questions. But you are not that old, so you certainly do not know the answers.
Have you gone into the place where I keep snow, or have you visited the place where I keep hail?
I keep snow and hail so that I can use them to defeat one of the armies when people are fighting wars.
Would you know how to get to the place where the sun should rise each morning? Would you know where the east wind should begin to blow over the earth?
Could you make rain fall in a certain place? Could you make a rainstorm go in a certain direction
so that it would rain out in the desert, in a place where no one lives?
Would you be able to send rain there to water those barren areas where nothing has grown, so that grass would begin to grow again?
Do you even know where rain comes from? Do you know how dew forms on the ground overnight?
Do you know how water becomes ice in the winter? Do you know why dew turns into the frost that covers the ground in the winter?
Do you know why the surface of lakes freezes in the winter? You cannot see the water below the surface; it is as if there is a layer of stone on top of it.
Can you make stars cluster together, as they do in the cluster you call the Pleiades? Can you make stars move apart so that they no longer make constellations such as the one you call Orion?
Can you make the constellations of stars appear in the sky at the right time of the year? Can you make the Big Dipper with its handle appear in the right place in the sky?
Do you know how the sun, moon, and stars should move through the sky? Do you know how they should provide heat and light on the earth?
Could you shout an order up to a cloud to make it pour rain down on you?
Can you tell flashes of lightning to strike wherever you want? Would the lightning do what you commanded?
Can you determine where it should be cloudy and where it should be sunny?
Are you able to count how many clouds there are? Can you make it rain
after it has not rained for such a long time that the ground is hard and dry?

Suppose a lioness and her cubs were crouching in their den or hiding in some bushes, waiting for some animal to pass by that they could kill. Could you make an animal go by that the lioness could kill so that she and her cubs could eat the meat and not be hungry anymore?

Suppose some baby ravens in a nest were chirping loudly because they were hungry. Suppose they had not eaten in so long that they had become weak. Could you provide a dead animal whose meat the raven could bring home to its baby birds?
Job, can you tell when female mountain goats are about to give birth? Have you watched the wild deer while their calves were being born?
Do you know for how long these female animals will be pregnant? Do you know when they will have their babies?
They crouch down to give birth, and their babies come out.
The young animals grow up in the open fields. Once they are strong enough to leave their mothers, they do not return to them again.
Do you know why some donkeys wander around wild? Do you know why they are not still working for people?
I have given them a home in the desert plain. They are able to live in places where much grass does not grow.
These wild donkeys do not like the noise in the cities. In the desert, they do not have to listen to the shouts of those who used to force them to work.
They wander over the hills to find food. They look for any plant that they can eat.
There are also oxen that are wild. You could not get one of those to work for you! It would not stay penned up at night by the place where you put food for your animals!
You could not make a wild ox pull a plow so that it would dig furrows in your fields.
Even though a wild ox is very strong, you could not depend on it to do difficult farm work.
A wild ox would not help you to grow more crops than you could grow by yourself.
Now think about ostriches. They run very fast, flapping their wings as they go. But they do not take good care of their offspring.
Female ostriches are bad mothers, because lay their eggs and leave them on the ground. The eggs do stay warm in the sand.
But this is still not a good thing to do. Some wild animal could step on the eggs and crush them.

Ostriches do not care well for their chicks. They act as if the chicks do not belong to them. They do not seem to be concerned that their chicks might die and they would have laid their eggs for nothing.
Ostriches act this way because I did not give them good instincts. I did not enable them to understand how they should care for their eggs and chicks.
However, ostriches are still awesome birds. When they run, they can easily run faster than horses!
But I made horses to be very strong. I put beautiful flowing manes on their necks.
I enabled them to leap through the air as if they were locusts. They snort so loudly that they cause people to be afraid.
As horses prepare to rush into battle, they paw the ground, showing off their great strength.
Horses seem to disregard danger as they go bravely into battle. They do not run away when enemy soldiers attack them.
As horses run into battle, the quivers containing their riders’ arrows rattle against their sides. The spears and javelins that they are carrying flash in the sunlight.
Horses rush into battle as soon as an officer blows a horn to signal that the army should advance. The horses run very quickly, and they speedily reach the enemy lines.

When they hear someone blow the battle horn, horses neigh excitedly. They can smell a battle even from a distance. They hear commanders shouting orders to their soldiers {and they know the battle will begin soon}.

Now think about birds that hunt small animals and other birds. Do you know how hawks are able to stay in the air as if they were floating? Do you know how they sense when it is time to fly to a warmer place for the winter?
I gave eagles the ability to fly high up into the cliffs and build their nests there.
Eagles live on cliffs. They are safe among the high, pointed rocks there because no animals can get to them.
From that great height, eagles look for animals that they can kill and eat. They can see animals that are far away.
Eagles kill small animals and bring them back to their nests to feed their chicks. Eagles also go and eat dead bodies that they see lying on the ground.”
Yahweh continued to speak to Job. He said,
“Do you still think I am wrong and want to keep arguing with me? If you want to keep criticizing me, then answer the questions I have asked you!”
But Job replied to Yahweh,
“Now I realize how insignificant I am. I am not able to answer your questions. I will not say anything in response to them.
I have already said more than I should have said. So now I will say nothing more.”
Then Yahweh again spoke to Job from inside the storm. He said,
“I am going to ask you some more questions, so get ready to answer them directly.
Do you still want to govern the universe instead of me? Do you still want to insist that I am doing things wrong and that you would do them right?
Do you have the same amount of power as I do? Does your voice sound as loud as thunder, as mine does?
If you want to govern the universe, you must show that you are dignified and noble. You must show that your character is glorious and beautiful.
You must express holy wrath against the people who deserve it. You must recognize which people are being sinfully arrogant and take them out of important positions.
Yes, you must not allow arrogant people to remain in important positions. Destroy wicked people quickly!
Punish all of them by killing them. Then send them to the place where dead people go.
If you did that, I would congratulate you and admit that you could save yourself by your own ability.

{But to show you how insignificant you really are,} I want you to think about a great animal that I created, Behemoth. I made you, and I also made it. Even though this great beast has the size and strength to hunt and kill other animals, it eats plants as oxen do.
Think about how strong the legs of Behemoth are! And the muscles in its belly are very powerful.
Behemoth can make its tail as stiff as the branch of a cedar tree and hold it up in the air. It has very strong legs.
Its thigh bones are so strong that they are like tubes made of bronze. Its legs are so strong that they are like bars made of iron.
Behemoth is one of the strongest animals that I made. I gave it sharp tusks so that it could cut down plants and eat them.

It needs those tusks because it comes out of the river where it lives in order to eat the plants that grow nearby. But other animals do not have to be afraid of it, so those animals do not run away or hide.
Behemoth lies under the trees that grow near the river where it lives. It sometimes shelters in the tall reeds that grow in the swamps of the river.
Behemoth stays in the shade of trees that grow near the river. It stays in the midst of the trees that grow near the water.
Even when the river in which it lives become strong and turbulent, this does not disturb Behemoth. It does not mind even if the level of the water in the river rises very high.
No one could capture Behemoth even if he could get close enough to stand right in front of it. No one can make Behemoth a tame animal.
{And now I want you to think about another great animal that I created, Leviathan.} You cannot catch Leviathan with a fishhook, and you cannot tie rope around its jaws to hold them closed!
You cannot hook its jaws to catch it and then put cords through its nose to control it.
Leviathan would certainly not plead with you to act mercifully toward it! It would not use sweet talk to try to get you not to harm it!
Leviathan would certainly not make an agreement to work for you as your slave for as long as it lived!
You could not turn it into a pet, as people do with birds! You could not put a leash around its neck so that the young women in your household could take it for walks!

People who work together to catch fish could never catch Leviathan and then decide what share of it belonged to each of them. They would never get the chance to cut Leviathan into pieces and then sell its meat!
People cannot throw harpoons hard enough at Leviathan to pierce its hide! People cannot throw fishing spears into its head!
If you try to fight with Leviathan, it will give you a battle that you will never forget! You will never try to do that again!
It is useless even to hope to subdue Leviathan. Just the sight of it is enough to make a person become so afraid that he falls down.
No one is so foolhardy that he would wake up Leviathan if it were sleeping. {It would angrily attack him.} Since that is true, it is even more foolhardy to challenge me{, as you have done}.

{Even if people are righteous,} they have not done anything for me that obligates me to make only good things happen to them. Everything in the created world belongs to me{, so no one can give me anything that I have to repay.}
And now I want to speak to you further. {You said that you wanted to wake up Leviathan! As I said, that would be very foolish.} It has agile legs and great strength and a graceful shape.
It has a tough hide that no one can strip off. It has powerful jaws.
Those jaws have terrible teeth in them! No one can pry them open when they are closed{, and no one can release them when they bite onto something.}
It has rows of scales on its back with no gaps between them.
Those scales are so close together that it seems as if not even air can get between them.
Those scales join very closely to each other and they do not pull apart.
When Leviathan makes a loud sound, fire comes out of its mouth as well as noise. It has bright, scary eyes that seem to glow with fire.
When it breathes, it shoots out flames and fiery sparks.
Smoke pours out of its nostrils the way steam pours out of a pot of boiling water over a hot fire.
Flames shoot out from its mouth, so when it breathes on wood, the wood catches fire.
Its neck is very strong. Wherever it goes, it makes people very afraid.
Leviathan does not have a soft belly as other animals do. Scales wrap around its belly and hold it tightly to its body.
It does not feel any compassion, any more than a stone would feel compassion or the lower millstone on which people grind grain would feel compassion.
When Leviathan rises up out of the ocean, the bravest people become terrified. When sailors see it churning up the water, they sail away as fast as they can.
People cannot injure it with swords. They cannot injure it with spears, arrows, or other weapons that have sharp points, either.
An iron weapon could not hurt it any more than straw could. A bronze weapon could not hurt it any more than a weapon made of rotten wood.
Shooting arrows at it does not cause it to flee. Hurling stones at it from a sling is like hurling bits of chaff at it.
A club that someone might use against it would not hurt it any more than chaff would. It can ignore any spear that someone might throw at it.
Scales as sharp as broken pieces of pottery cover its belly. When it drags itself through the mud, these scales tear up the ground.
As it swims through the deep water of the ocean, it churns it into foam, as if it were boiling water or ointment that someone was stirring.
As it swims through the water, it creates a glistening wake. The churning water is like white hair on top of the deep sea.
There is nothing in the world like Leviathan. I created it in such a way that it would not be afraid of anything.
Nothing else scares it, no matter how powerful that thing may be. It is greater than the greatest of other creatures.”
Then Job replied to Yahweh. He said,
“Now I realize that you can do anything you want. No one can stop you from doing what you want to do.

You told me that I had been speaking ignorantly, and that as a result, I was making it harder for people to understand your actions. I will admit that I was speaking about things that I did not understand. Those things were very amazing, and I did not really know what I was talking about.

You told me that I should listen and let you talk because you were going to ask me some questions. You wanted me to try to answer them. {But I will admit that I am not able to answer the questions you asked.}
I had previously heard many things about you. But now I have actually seen you!
Therefore I am ashamed of myself for what I said. I am sitting in dust and ashes to show that I am sorry for what I said.”

When Yahweh had finished speaking with Job, he spoke to Eliphaz, Job’s friend from the town of Teman. He said, “I am very angry with you and your two friends. I am angry because you did not say true things about me the way Job did. He serves me faithfully.

So now you must bring seven young bulls and seven rams to Job, that man who serves me faithfully. While he is with you, kill these animals and burn them as a sacrifice for yourselves. Then Job will pray for you, and I will do what he asks me to do for you. I will not punish you for speaking foolishly about me. You deserve for me to punish you because you did not say the right things about me as Job did. He serves me faithfully.”

So Eliphaz, Job’s friend from the town of Teman; Bildad, Job’s friend from the Shuhite people group; and Zophar, Job’s friend from the town of Naamah, did what Yahweh had commanded them to do. Then Job prayed for his friends, and Yahweh forgave them as Job asked him to do.
After Job had prayed for his three friends, Yahweh healed him and made him wealthy again. Yahweh gave him twice as much wealth as he had before.

Then Job’s family and friends came to his house and had a feast with him. All of his brothers and sisters came, and all of his former acquaintances also came. They cheered him up now that all of the troubles were over that Yahweh had allowed to happen to him. Each of them gave Job a valuable piece of silver and a gold earring.
Yahweh blessed Job more in the second part of his life than he had blessed him in the first part of his life. Job acquired 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 pairs of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.
Job also had seven more sons and three more daughters.
He named the first daughter Jemimah. He named the second daughter Keziah. And he named the third daughter Keren Happuch.
Job’s three daughters were the most beautiful women in the whole land of Uz. As their father, Job declared that his daughters would each receive an inheritance from him, just as their brothers would.

After God restored Job’s prosperity, he lived for 140 more years. His new children had children of their own. Then his grandchildren had children of their own, so Job was even able to get to know his great-grandchildren.
Job finally died after living a good long life.
